articleTitle: Data Modeling for Productive Asset and Supporting Asset
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Asset management is an essential thing that needs to be governed by an organization or company, mainly if it is supported using an information system. However, currently, most asset management information systems are specified for recording or inventorying assets only. The recorded data is also specified to asset attributes and their metadata. If the asset management information system can be prepared using a more comprehensive approach, the asset management information system built can be adjusted to the organization's goals. Recording assets is not just a database but can be linked to what the organization wants to achieve and from the processes in it. This paper proposes how to derive data modeling for asset management using an approach to aligning organizational goals and critical processes. Besides that, it is also seen from the classification of assets that the mapping of business processes becomes more precise. One of the proposed classifications is the classification of productive assets and supporting assets. The result is an asset mapping model based on the core process organization and the asset entities that appear in it.

articleTitle: Sleep Stage Identification of Split Wave EEG Signals Using CNN-RNN
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Sleep disturbance can indeed have a profound impact on various aspects of health and well-being. Monitoring sleep quality and detecting sleep disorders are crucial to maintaining overall health. EEG data plays a significant role in understanding sleep patterns and identifying different sleep stages. Sleep is divided into five levels: Awake, Rapid eye movement (REM), Non-REM 1, Non-REM 2, and Non-REM 3. This research aims to improve the accuracy of identifying sleep levels from EEG signals by dividing the EEG signal into specific frequency bands (Delta, Theta, Alpha, Beta waves) using a Wavelet filter and then applying a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) in parallel for sleep level identification. The experimental results showed that the split signal waves approach achieved an accuracy of 98.34%, indicating a promising advancement in sleep stage identification. This high accuracy is particularly impressive, especially compared to the accuracy achieved using simultaneous signal processing.

articleTitle: Texture-Based Dipterocarpaceae Trunk Classification Using Two Stage Transfer Learning of VGG16
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The significance of plant identification has already been recognized by academia and industry. There were several attempts to utilize leaves and flowers for identification. However, the trunk also could be beneficial, especially for tall trees. This research focuses on the Dipterocarpaceae family classification that could attain heights between 70 and 85 meters. Leveraging deep learning using VGG16 architecture, this study proposes a two-stage transfer learning strategy. In the first stage, the pre-trained VGG16 is fine-tuned by modifying only the classification layer while keeping the feature layer frozen. The second stage involves unfreezing the last three convolutional layers to adapt the model more specifically to Dipterocarpaceae trunk classification. A dataset containing 681 images of different Dipterocarp species was collected. Through experimentation, the proposed method achieves a remarkable accuracy of 97.09% on the testing set, outperforming traditional transfer learning method. This research highlights the approach's potential for accurate species identification, offering benefits to conservation and ecological studies by enabling rapid and reliable classification of tree species based on trunk texture images.

articleTitle: Stardist Segmentation to Determine the Printout Characteristics of Different Printers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The simplicity papers may be printed has increased illegal activities such as document forgery. Better ways to distinguish between fake and real documents are necessary to overcome this issue. This paper proposes a unique approach for reliably identifying printer sources. This study applied the Arabic letter from three different types of printers such as HP Laserjet P2010, HP LaserJet 2200dn, and LaserJet CP3525dn. The proposed method to identify the difference is by implementing Stardist technique. The result shows that each printer's threshold, probability, distance, and label image has a different pattern. From the result of mean and area in the image using Stardist can be seen that some printers as LJ-3525 have a lower value than others.

articleTitle: Smart Plant Monitoring System with Adaptive Linear Regression Predictor for Predicting Next Watering Time
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The demand for an efficient and automated solution to address the challenge of plant care in the face of limited human availability has led to the development of automatic watering systems. This system utilizes data from soil moisture, light intensity, and temperature sensors to provide efficient and effective plant care. When the system detects dry soil conditions, it initiates watering, ensuring that plants receive the necessary water for optimal growth. To further optimize watering cycles, the system incorporates adaptive linear regression. By analyzing historical data on soil moisture, the system estimates the next watering cycle. The simulations demonstrate that the predictor algorithm effectively handles soil moisture cases that increase while providing better estimation results when soil moisture decreases linearly. In essence, this means that the system can effectively adapt to changing conditions, ensuring that the right amount of water is delivered to the plants precisely when it's needed, thereby enhancing plant health and growth while optimizing water usage. This capability holds great promise for sustainable and efficient plant care, especially in situations where resources are limited or where environmentally responsible practices are essential.

articleTitle: Optimization of Random Forest Algorithm for Paddy Growth Stage Classification Using Bayesian Optimization and Oversampling
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Remote sensing and machine learning (ML) technologies that have developed very rapidly allow data retrieval and processing for monitoring paddy field conditions with minimal human intervention. One of the machine learning algorithms that is widely used for paddy growth stage classification is Random Forest. This study rebuilt the Random Forest model with datasets derived from a combination of Area Sample Framework (KSA) data and Sentinel-1A imagery attributes. The highest accuracy result by this model is still <60%. Therefore, this study aims to examine how to optimize the Random Forest algorithm in classifying paddy growth stages. The optimization method used is to perform hyperparameter tuning with the Bayesian Optimization method and handle imbalanced data with oversampling techniques. As a result, the f1-score of Random Forest Optimization Model with Bayesian Optimization and oversampling increase in average of 6% and has a trend similar to the Random Forest baseline model with and produces a stable f1-score under varying dataset conditions.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of Political Party News on the Online News Portal Detik.com Using LSTM and CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The online news portal Detik.com contains numerous articles discussing specific political parties. The development of a sentiment analysis model can be used to analyze political party news data on Detik.com and identify the sentiments expressed in the data. Web scraping method was employed to gather a dataset consisting of 19,463 rows. The data labeling process was conducted in four stages by multiple individuals. Sentiment analysis of the political party news data from Detik.com utilized a combination of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models, along with Word2Vec and FastText word embedding vectors. The Word2Vec-CNN-LSTM model achieved the highest average accuracy, which was 69.39%. The same model also attained the highest maximum accuracy, reaching 70.46%. Evaluation of the model revealed that the combination of LSTM and CNN models performed exceptionally well on news articles with a large number of relevant sentiment words, but exhibited lower accuracy on articles with fewer relevant sentiment words. FastText word embedding vectors demonstrated better performance in predicting non-neutral labeled text data, while Word2Vec exhibited superior performance in predicting neutral text data.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Paddy Growth Stage Classification Using Stacking CART and Random Forest Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Indonesia is an agricultural country with one of its main agricultural commodities being rice. One of the areas that is the center of rice cultivation in Indonesia, especially on Java Island, is the Karawang Regency. There are several methods of measuring rice production data, one of which is the ASF statistical method. Apart from using these statistical methods, there are several studies showing that machine learning models can be developed to predict paddy growth stage precisely and accurately. This research uses Sentinel-1A image data which is extrapolated with ASF samples which are then oversampled as an imbalance data handling method. In this study, the development of the CART algorithm was carried out by using parameters maxnodes value of 1000 and a minleafpopulation of 1. Furthermore, the development of a stacking CART was carried out with the meta learner being a random forest. The results of this study indicate that when oversampling is applied to the data, Pearson Correlations in the estimated areas from the CART Method of classes V1 (Early Vegetative), V2 (Late Vegetative), G (Generative), and P&PL (Harvest and Land Preparation) toward estimated area derived from area sampling frame (ASF) method have reduced with deviation average is 0.21195 compared to Pearson Correlation in the estimated area using the same methods without oversampling the data. In addition, area estimation using the stacking CART+RF method shows an increase in Pearson correlation with an average of 0.26612 compared to the area estimation results using the CART method with oversampled data.

articleTitle: A Novel Multi-Modal Deep Learning Method for Fish's Appetite Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: In aquaculture, feeding cost usually takes a lot from the total budget. However, a significant portion of the feed often gets uneaten by the fish. To overcome this problem, many ways have been developed using artificial intelligence to detect fish's appetite levels. In this paper, a deep learning model using multi-modal sensors is implemented to detect fish's appetite level based on its visual and the aquarium's water movement. We propose the combination R(2+1)D-CNN and 1D-ANN to process the sensor data, in the form of video streams and accelerometer signals, respectively. Based on the result, this model significantly increases the accuracy of the inference (from 86.71% to 91.84% testing accuracy) without adding many learning parameters (from 1,777,186 to 1,833,008 parameters), compared to the model using a single-modal deep learning model with the camera.

articleTitle: Optimization of Switched Reluctance Motor for Two Wheels Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Switched reluctance motor (SRM) have become widely used for many application in recent years due to its simple structure. However, recent trend in two wheels electric vehicle application still tends toward the use of brushless DC (BLDC) motor as its main propulsion system. Thus, in this paper, design and analysis of a switched reluctance motor for the application of a two wheels electric vehicle were discussed and further investigated. Analysis of the switched reluctance motor design was performed using software model representation in FEA software. Comparative study of the switched reluctance motor with a brushless DC motor for the application of an two wheels electric vehicle was presented. Optimization of the switched reluctance motor were also performed to further improve the performance of the initial design. From the result, it was found that the switched reluctance motor manage to gives similar performance in terms of its efficiency and torque output as compared to the brushless DC motor and can be considered as a potential replacement for the two wheels electric vehicle application.

articleTitle: Unleashing the Impact of IT Integration Implementation in Public Sector Organizations Through the Lens of TOE: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive review of the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) model, which is a framework often used to analyze the impact of IT integration implementation in organizations. The TOE model, developed by Tornatzky and Fleischer in 1990, focuses on understanding the adoption and implementation of technological innovations by considering three key aspects: the technological context, organizational context, and environmental context. This review highlights the strengths, limitations, and suitability of the TOE model in the context of IT integration implementation within public sector organizations to improve service delivery.

articleTitle: A Real Time Implementation of SpectroNet for Music Player Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Keyword Spotting(KWS), which refers to the task of recognizing spoken words out of a small database of words, has become one of the most popular research topics. After the emergence of deep learning architectures, such as Convolutional Neural Network(CNN) and Reccurent Neural Network(RNN), works have been done to apply these architectures to Keyword Spotting problems. Keyword Spotting can have different topics/themes, such as home automation, robot control, etc. In this paper, music player is chosen as the topic of the KWS. A novel database will be created to test the system. The network chosen to implement this is SpectroNet, which is a low-complexity hybrid CNN-RNN architecture based on the DenseNet architecture.

articleTitle: GDP: Group-Based Differential Privacy Framework for Secure Process Mining in the Internet of Medical Things
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: With the widespread adoption of Internet of Things (IoTs) technology in the healthcare domain, the Internet of Medical Things (IoMTs) has emerged as a promising paradigm for improving patient care and healthcare outcomes. IoMT generates vast amounts of data, including process logs. Therefore, Process Mining (PM) is a potential approach that can provide valuable insights into healthcare processes for several optimizations. The analysis of such sensitive data through PM raises privacy and security concerns. However, using PM for specific data allows IoMTs to secure the sensitive data. Therefore, this paper aims to evaluate existing PM algorithms, for behavior after adding noise in data without affecting PM results. Differential Privacy (DP) is a widely recognized privacy-preserving technique that provides strong privacy guarantees by injecting random noise into data. Therefore, this research presents a framework, called Group-based DP (GDP) for PM to protect the privacy of healthcare data in specific columns which are neither activity nor class ID. This study includes evaluation of prominent PM algorithms, including, Alpha algorithm, Heuristics algorithm, inductive algorithm, correlation mining algorithm and footprints algorithm. Furthermore, we suggested pertinent advanced research directions concerning real-world requirements.

articleTitle: Current Control Comparison Using Conventional and Multi Resonant PI in Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The current control system is a necessary system to be able to utilize renewable energy, where the current controller compares the current connected to the power grid with the reference current. A power conversion system is needed to connect the energy storage system to the grid. The power conversion that matches this system is by using an inverter. Inverters with current controllers are needed to regulate the current entering the grid because the power from the inverter is injected into the power grid and the voltage can be obtained from the grid, so what can be controlled is the current that goes into the grid. Inverters can be controlled with conventional PI current controllers and multiresonant PI current control. Multiresonant PI control can be designed using the Naslin Polynomial method by determining the open loop and closed loop of the transfer function, so that the Kp and Ki values are obtained according to the required system. Conventional PI current control method and multiresonant PI are successful in controlling the inverter output. In this study, it was found that multiresonant PI current control and conventional PI can stabilize the system quickly in the event of load changes. Multiresonant PI and conventional PI have no steady state error, but conventional PI has steady state error when starting the system. The multiresonant PI current controller has a lower current ripple effect than the conventional PI controller.

articleTitle: PCA-SVM for a Lightweight ASL Hand Gesture Image Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Other studies have previously researched creating a new dataset called Gesture Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology (MNIST Gesture), similar to the MNIST dataset for American sign language (ASL) hand gestures. Several methods, such as long short-term memory (LSTM), have been used for gesture detection on the dataset. However, there is a research opportunity to provide a learning model that requires less training data. Our research aim is to use PCA-SVM for lightweight hand gesture recognition. The first step of our research is to collect the MNIST Gesture dataset from Kaggle. Then, we do preprocessing and prediction model training. We then compare PCA with the mean decrease in impurity (MDI) and the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) method in their performance to reduce dataset dimensions in the SVM training process. Lastly, we compare our proposed model with two state-of-the-art benchmark models: long short-term memory (LSTM) and convolutional neural network (CNN). The test results show that the optimum number of PCA-SVM principal components in ASL hand gesture recognition is 50. Then, PCA performs better than MDI and LASSO on dimension reduction with an SVM model. Finally, the PCA-SVM model bests LSTM in hand gesture recognition by accuracy, precision, recall, and f1-score. However, PCA-SVM and CNN both have an accuracy higher than 0.99. On the other hand, PCA-SVM is more lightweight than CNN because it has a shorter training time and testing time, namely 3.5 s and 0.2 s, respectively.

articleTitle: Comparation Classification of EMG Signals in the Time Domain and Time-Frequency Domain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Electromyography (EMG) has been used extensively in motion recognition for rehabilitation or prosthetic control. One of the challenges in EMG-based motion recognition is the effective and accurate classification of EMG signals. In this study, we compare the performance of EMG signal classification between feature extraction in the time domain and time-frequency domain. EMG signal data was obtained from a public dataset with a total of 36 subjects. The feature extraction method in the time domain will use statistical features such as root mean square (RMS), mean absolute value (MAV), variance (VAR), zero crossing (ZC), and Integrated EMG (IEMG), while the method in the time-frequency domain will use the wavelet transform (WT). EMG signal classification will be carried out using several classifiers including Support vector machines, K-NN (k-Nearest Neighbor), Decision Tree (DT), and Random Forest (RF). The results showed that the method with feature extraction in the time-frequency domain was significantly better than the method in the time domain in classifying EMG signals using a random forest classifier with a higher classification accuracy ratio (99.95% vs. 95.50%). The results of this study can be used as a reference in selecting a more accurate and effective EMG signal classification method in motion recognition during rehabilitation or prosthetic control.

articleTitle: Enhancing Hierarchical CNN Via Pathway Loss and Reference Forwarding Synergy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Computer vision applications have been widely used in critical areas however its reliability is hampered by low accuracy when dealing with small objects. As the internal information for small objects is limited by its pixels, addition of external information from the object context is important to determine object identity. Context features that are shared among objects can be used to group and label them hierarchically. It will then be used to improve classification by reducing the search space and linking the object's general feature or function. Hierarchical-based CNN uses a hierarchy of labels with multi-level classifiers in classification of simpler coarser level before tackling more complex classification on finer level. However, the current implementation of hierarchical CNN keeps information between levels isolated from each other thus limiting the potential of its structure. Improvement is made towards the loss function with the addition of pathway loss where the hierarchy pathway from coarse to fine is considered on each classifier branch. Additionally, we introduce the reference forwarding function, which transfers crucial information learned from previous layers to the subsequent finer ones, thereby further improving the classification accuracy. Proof of concept experiments on CIFAR-100 dataset shows each of the proposed innovations improve accuracy compared to baseline model and the overall combinations synergize well with each other, achieving the best result with improvement of almost 8%.

articleTitle: RCC-INC Hybrid MPPT
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Green energy is one of the most popular topics. The energy resource with minimum pollutants or environmentally friendly can be generated by hydropower, solar power, and many other resources. Solar energy is one of the most potential electric power sources. The PV module extracts an electric current that flows through the buck converter connected to the load. Optimization of solar energy systems has become important in a solar power plant. MPPT algorithm has become the key to optimizing power extraction. Incremental conductance (InC) is a popular MPPT algorithm. InC tracks MPP and generates PWM to control the buck converter. The advantages of InC are high-accuracy MPPT and small oscillation and the disadvantages are tracking speed of MPP. This algorithm has more power loss when the system starts and tracks MPP. Another algorithm such as Ripple Correlation Control (RCC) has the advantage fast in tracking MPP but it has lower accuracy in tracking MPP. This research resolves the InC's tracking speed MPP and reduces the power loss by a combined Ripple Correlation Control (RCC) MPPT algorithm. The result is tracking speed is 0.19 ms or 16 percent faster than conventional and reduces 4.1 watts or 3 percent power loss.

articleTitle: Design of the Bontocani Health Center Service Application: A Proposed Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Indonesia is a country that has 273 million people with uneven population distribution. Bontocani District is one of the areas in South Sulawesi with one health center and three auxiliary health centers, with an average expedition time of about 120 minutes to reach a health facility. In addition, road access to health facilities is also quite challenging in certain conditions, like rain. Therefore, web and Android-based applications are needed to make it easier for people to obtain health services. Clinical teleconsultation is an option to make it easier for people to get a diagnosis. This paper proposes a design of Android and web-based clinical teleconsultation applications for the Community Health centers in Indonesia. In the future, this health center information system can also be held in other health center and integrated with fellow health centers in one district and even the province to get better patient care.

articleTitle: Managing Security Hazards in BYOD: A Comparative Analysis of Artificial Intelligent Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) policies have gained popularity in organizations, offering flexibility and increased productivity. However, they also introduce security hazards that pose risks to sensitive data and systems such as data leakage, weak authentication, malware and viruses, unsecured Wi-Fi networks, device loss or theft, and compliance issues. These problems continuously affect to the organization. Therefore, these problems can be solved by adopting artificial intelligent (AI) techniques. This paper investigates the possibility of potential solutions by adopting AI techniques such as machine learning-based anomaly detection, behavior analysis, predictive analytics, and natural language processing will be examined as potential solutions. The objective of this paper is to identify and compare various AI techniques in addressing the security hazards associated with BYOD. The methodology involves a comprehensive review of relevant articles and research papers to gather insight findings. The results of this research will provide a summary of available AI techniques in monitoring the BYOD security hazards.

articleTitle: Interactive STEM in Cyber Awareness Learning System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The internet and computer applications are useful to everyday life but without proper control, it can threaten everyone's life. Now, the dependence on the use of internet and social media has opened the risk to the new threat which is cybercrime. Cybercrime is a crime through the use of computers, where it has become a major challenge faced globally. Therefore they (especially students) need to be exposed to knowledge about cybercrimes such as cyber bullying, cyber stalking, cyber harassment, identity theft, and others. Awareness of this crime is necessary so that they can provide preventive measures by controlling themselves from getting caught up in this crime. Therefore, a cyber education module that is compatible with Malaysians' culture needs to be developed. The importance of cyber education among school students has attracted the interest of many parties. However, the educational approach is geared towards traditional methods through lectures or informal learning. Therefore, the cyber learning package is necessary to give exposure to students in increasing their awareness of the cybercrime threats. Based on reviews on the development of cyber education, until today there has been no comprehensive effort in developing interactive cyber learning package that are suitable for Malaysians' culture. This study used STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) learning approach to increase student motivation in cyber education. To support STEM approach, five learning principles of 5E (namely engage, explore, explain, elaborate, and evaluate) is adopted. The advantage of using this learning principle is it encourages and motivates students in learning as well as give proper guidance in skill development. To adopt STEM approach, a learning model is proposed that consists of 5E learning principles in cyber education.

articleTitle: World Education Website Localization Using A Culture-Based Design Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: To observe the effect of a culture-based design approach in developing a web-based application for Indonesian citizens, as well as attempt to increase the efficiency and satisfaction of its usage, the World Education website was localized according to a culture-based process model. The website was localized in two iterations, during which six primary features were designed and implemented. Cultural considerations during the development process include local user observation, local site audit, and a cultural analysis based on Hofstede's model. The localized website was tested against the original website during the final iteration, in which an increase in usability and user experience goal scores, as well as the overall satisfaction of the website's interface was observed.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Line Follower for Adaptive Headlight
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: This project aims to design and implement a Line Follower system for Adaptive Headlights. Adaptive Headlights are a technology in vehicles that regulates the angle and intensity of the headlights based on the center line of the road or the direction of the vehicle in front. In developing autonomous vehicles is their ability to accurately follow lines on the road. To overcome this problem, we introduced the Line Follower with Adaptive Headlight (LFAH) system, which combines reliable line follower technology with automatically adjustable headlights. The LFAH system is designed to enable autonomous vehicles to follow paths with precision. The line follower algorithm allows vehicles to detect and follow lines on the roadway with high accuracy. The Adaptive Headlight on the LFAH uses various sensors, including a line follower sensor and a proximity sensor. When the vehicle approaches the area the headlights will automatically turn down so that they can optimize the lighting. This not only improves safety but also allows the vehicle to follow the path better at night. Field trial results show that the LFAH system can successfully follow lines in a wide range of lighting conditions. LFAH systems with Adaptive Headlights have great potential to improve the safety and performance of autonomous vehicles on the road. We hope that this research will make a positive contribution to the future development of autonomous vehicle technology.

articleTitle: Automatic Heliostat Directing System Based On Microcontroller ESP32
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Solar energy is one of the most abundant sources of renewable energy in Indonesia. Solar energy is now typically harnessed using solar panels, but the low efficiency of photovoltaic cells requires the development of other alternatives. The heliostat is a sunlight directing device with mirrors that can be used in a concentrated solar power system. Current heliostats require high capital investment due to their large frames and expensive components. This research was undertaken to develop a lower cost heliostat using a smaller frame, ESP32 microcontroller, servo motor and low-cost components. The position of the sun can be determined using an algorithm based on the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) solar calculator, and the mirror is moved to maintain the sun's reflection on a target. The result of this research is a set of heliostat prototypes consisting of the frame and control system. Tests were carried out to test the performance of the designed heliostat and it was found that the heliostat has an accuracy of about 60 cm and can raise temperatures up to 3.41°C. The conclusion is that the heliostat can be used in a concentrated solar power system to heat boilers in solar power towers.

articleTitle: Image Enhancement for Breast Cancer Based on Image Contrast, Interpolation and Filtering
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The present work proposes a methodology for enhancing images by the application of contrast adjustment, interpolation techniques, and filtering algorithms. Techniques employ a dual-system approach. The first image enhancement technique commonly involves contrast augmentation, bicubic interpolation, and the application of a median filter for denoising purposes. The second technique involves bicubic interpolation and contrast enhancement. The suggested methodology enhances the quality of images, as evidenced by the achieved Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) values of 0.46 dB, Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) values of 0.459 dB, Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) values of 0.009, and Mean Squared Error (MSE) values of 1.32E-04. The suggested method utilizes both objective and subjective measures to depict the outcomes of image enhancement. These metrics are also used to compare the results with other methods. The strategy under consideration takes into account more intricate details, heightened contrast, and enhanced edge definition, leading to a superior image outcome compared to the method being compared.

articleTitle: Modeling Land Classification and Corn Planting Phases Using KSA Observation Points with CNN and SMOTE Hybrid Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: In 2020, BPS and BPPT developed an Area Sampling Survey (KSA) for maize to obtain accurate and precise food security data. On the other hand, the KSA Survey has several weaknesses in its application, one of which is the KSA Survey not being able to explore areas that can not be reached, and so on. To overcome this problem, we propose to use of remote sensing as a data collection technique. This study aims to obtain the best maize land classification model and corn planting phase using machine learning, deep learning, and the SMOTE method. The results showed that the best model for land classification and maize planting phase were CNN-1D-SMOTE 2 labels with 85% accuracy, 79% sensitivity, 63% precision, and f1-score 70% and SVM without SMOTE 58% accuracy, respectively. Sensitivity 59.5%, precision 54%, and f1-score 55.7%. The estimated corn planting area for 2021 is 36,049.15 ha.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Passive Sonar Prototype for Ship Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Indonesia is the largest archipelagic country in the world. The geographical location of Indonesia, which consists of islands and many straits, has resulted in smuggling and the entry of foreign ships. Increasing the security of the sea area needs to be improved, one of which is by advancing technology. Passive sonar is a technology that can detect foreign ships without being noticed by the target. The acoustic signal emitted by the ship can be used in passive sonar to detect the direction of the ship's arrival. In this research, a passive sonar prototype was developed using the Uniform Circular Array (UCA) model and a power comparison algorithm to detect the arrival direction of ships, a frequency of 1 kHz is assumed to be an acoustic signal emitted by a ship. The developed passive sonar prototype can detect acoustic signals in the water medium. The power comparison algorithm in air medium has the lowest average error at a distance of 0.6 m at an angle of 360° with a value of 0.3201 and at a distance of 1.2 m at an angle of 90° with a value of 0.2585.

articleTitle: Smartphone-Integrated Reverse Lens Hemocount Microscope for Red Blood Cell Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Anemia, a prevalent global medical condition affecting approximately 33% of the world's population in 2015 and 32% of Indonesian adolescents in 2018, is characterized by a reduction in red blood cell count or hemoglobin levels, resulting in diminished oxygen-carrying capacity within the bloodstream. The conventional method for detecting anemia involves Complete Blood Count (CBC), which demands specialized hematology analyzers and substantial time. In response to these constraints, the Hemocount, a portable microscope utilizing the reverse lens technique, was developed to capture high-quality images of red blood cells. This innovative approach requires blood sample standardization for optimal Hemocount performance. The technique involves inverting the mobile camera lens, aligning the sensor focus with the sample, while a preparation table and light source illuminate from below. Experiments with various lens, table, and light source configurations identified the optimal setup as employing the front camera lens from an iPhone 5s, a transparent table, and a cool white light source, yielding a digital image resolution of 42.19 nm/px. This resolution allows for blood cell detection within the size range of 165.92 px to 189.62 px. For optimal results when using Hemocount, a recommended blood concentration of 50% minimizes standard deviation, while concentrations of 30% maximize the correlation coefficient R, and 25% yield clear images by preventing red blood cell enlargement due to osmosis.

articleTitle: Stator and Rotor Pole Combination in Switched Reluctance Motors for Electric Motorcycle Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: With the increase of switched reluctance motor (SRM) popularity as viable replacement for permanent magnet motor, there are still hurdles to be overcome before this type motor could fully adopted in general use. One of the hurdles of SRM is high torque ripple which is potentially increase the noise level. This paper discusses the comparison of 3 SRMs design for 3 kW electric motorcycle application with stator and rotor configuration variation, such as 6/4, 12/8, and 18/12 poles. The 3 SRMs are designed in identical outer stator diameter and stack length. It is concluded that 12/8 pole combination is the most optimal design providing the highest average torque, optimal torque ripple, and optimal current requirement.

articleTitle: A Study of Mobile Application Accessibility Interface for Quranic Braille Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The widespread availability of mobile technology and increased smartphone usage present an opportunity to significantly improve Quranic Braille learning for blind and visually impaired (BVI) individuals through mobile applications (apps). By integrating with braille assistive devices, offering text-to-speech functionality and providing interactive learning experiences, mobile applications can greatly enhance the learning process. However, while studies on the development of mobile applications exist, there is a limited body of research focused on the design aspects of mobile apps to learn Quranic Braille. Thus, the aim of this study is to develop a user-centred mobile app focuses on the user interface (UI) that is tailored to the needs of BVI individuals to learn Quranic Braille. We developed a prototype for learning Quranic Braille that consist of an assistive device and a mobile application. This prototype is used to collect user requirements and validate design decisions. By actively involving BVI individuals, we gather valuable feedback that will help shape the development of the application. The study focuses on evaluating the usability and effectiveness of the mobile app's user interface with a touchscreen. The findings of this study indicate that a mobile app for learning Quranic Braille is potentially useful and worthy of further exploration. Further study is necessary to develop and refine interface design for BVI individuals, including the optimal use of UI adaptation to learn Quranic Braille.

articleTitle: Analysis of Optimizer Effects on CNN Model for Defect Identification in Welding Results of A 106 Grade B Carbon Steel Pipe
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Welding is one of the sectors that play a crucial role in supporting the rapid development of infrastructure. However, in the process, many defects occur that sometimes escape inspection and will lead to damage in building construction. The purpose of conducting this research is to investigate the influence of optimization methods on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models in detecting the quality of welding results based on three conditions: Normal, Excessive Reinforcement, and Undercut. The area to be detected is a portion of the welding result with a circular welding path around a full A106 Grade B carbon steel pipe. The image capture process is carried out using a digital camera mounted on a tool for rotating around the pipe to follow the welding path. The captured image result of 3024 x 3024 pixels is first processed by converting RGB to grayscale. Afterwards, the image is resized to a smaller scale of 128 x 128 pixels to accelerate the training process. Finally, the training and testing processes are conducted using a CNN model. In the CNN model, there are several optimizers such as SGDM, Rmsrop, and Adam. In this study, a comparison is conducted to find the best optimizer in an effort to minimize the occurrence of overfitting as well as achieve optimal detection accuracy. For optimal detection, a dataset of 300 images is required, consisting of: 100 Normal images, 100 Excess Reinforcement images, and 100 Undercut images.

articleTitle: Analysing Imbalanced Dataset for Postgraduate Student Dropout Using Predictive Analytics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Higher educational institutions face problems with increasing student dropout rates. Past research proposed multiple approaches, such as data mining, to solve this issue. However, the prediction model's ability to determine university students' dropout rate is still in its infancy. We explored various feature selection strategies (filter, wrapper and embedded) on postgraduate studies data from a public university. The dataset is imbalanced, and most of the class is students who finished their studies. The minority class is for students who have not completed their studies. The study applied an oversampling method named SMOTE on the imbalanced data in training to enable the classification algorithm to learn from a balanced dataset, thus minimising overfitting. Five supervised algorithms, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Naive Bayes, Multi-Layer Perceptron and Logistic Regression, were evaluated for the predictive model. The result shows that Random Forest is the best classification algorithm for the dataset. Random Forest produces the highest accuracy value of 100% when using the filter and embedded method and 99.878% when using the wrapper method when using test data.

articleTitle: Underwater Scanning Using LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The underwater vehicle-manipulator system (UVMS) is a typical platform for carrying sensors of underwater scanning. One of these sensors is Light Detection And Ranging (LiDAR). One of the further developments of LiDAR is Oceanic LiDAR or O-LiDAR. Compared with acoustic methods, optical methods which LiDAR has classified provide high resolution and accuracy. Our goal is to develop a LiDAR sensor to be able to scan underwater surfaces and integrate them into UVMS. There are 2 methods that we use, namely the submerged method and the airborne method. The Submerged LiDAR Scanning method is to insert the device into a watertight container, which is then placed in the water with the object to be detected. The Airborne LiDAR Scanning method is different from the previous method. In this method, the device is not placed in a special container, but placed above the water surface. In testing, we used 2 LiDAR sensors, the RPLiDAR Slamtec A2M8 and iPhone LiDAR. After testing with the submerged method, it turns out that the two sensors cannot detect objects. There is a possibility that the laser beam failed to penetrate the container. Then testing was carried out using the airborne method, but the results still failed to detect the object. Our hypothesis regarding the cause of the failure of the sensor to detect objects in the water is due to the water refraction factor and also the color of the laser light used. Based on these results and discussions, it can be concluded that the LiDAR A2M8 and iPhone LiDAR are not able to detect objects in the water.

articleTitle: Multi-Feature Extraction EMG For Classification of Finger Movement
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Many studies using EMG have been carried out, one example is the detection of hand movements with EMG. In general, research on hand movement detection uses MyoArmband as a module for recording EMG data. One of the obstacles to using the MyoArmband is that it's quite expensive and there are quite a lot of channels up to eight channels. Therefore, this study presents a comparison of the classification of five finger movements using KNN, Decision Tree, and Random Forest using only 3 EMG channels in the forearm muscles. In addition, this study also compares and combines the use of four feature extraction with Time-Domain such as RMS, VAR, MAV, and IEMG and compares the effect of using data transformation using Standardscaller on finger movement classification performance. The result of this study is that the addition of features can increase the accuracy value obtained. The best combination in this model is the RMS + MAAV + VAR feature with an accuracy of 95.15%, a precision of 95.15%, a sensitivity of 95.2%, and a specificity of 98.8%. In addition, the use of data transformation does not really affect the RF model.

articleTitle: Design of Fuse Cut Out (FCO) Detection Tools Break-Up on Internet of Things-Based Distribution Substations to Speed up Response Time of Disorders
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The distribution system is the most important system in the electric power system. In maintaining reliability and providing the best service to its customers, Indonesian electrical company (PT. PLN) prepares an electricity service officer who is ready 24 hours to handle disturbances that occur in the distribution system, one of which is disturbances in the distribution substation such as the breakdown of fuse link on fuse cut out (FCO) where the disorder is often known for a long time, which affects the response time (response time) of the officer in knowing the disturbance so that it has an impact on the voltage drop on the customer. In accordance with Indonesian national standard of electricity number 1 of 1995 which regulates the service voltage variation is determined at a minimum of 10% against nominal voltage, with this basis then if the voltage reads more than 10% with the parameter reading on the distribution substation every approximately twenty seconds, then the tool will send Indications of Fuse Link Breaking on FCO along with the size of the fuse link, current, voltage and address of the distribution substation to officers via message on the Telegram application in real time.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection System Architecture for Cyber-Physical System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) enable the control/monitor of physical process through some form of computational mechanism in the digital world, typically through feedback control. CPS is becoming more popular as it is used in many domains such as smart city, smart health, smart manufacturing, etc. However, their increasing popularity must be followed by addressing one of its important concerns, security. CPS failure in case of attack can impact the physical world, such as the Stuxnet attack that destroyed Iran's nuclear facility. That is why an extra effort is required to ensure protection of CPS from attack. In this paper, we present an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) architecture as IDS is a system that can be utilized to protect CPS. We also evaluate the proposed architecture when implementing it with our testbed CPS. The proposed IDS architecture encompasses the functionality to do data acquisition from CPS to IDS, data analysis to identify attack, response mechanism for detected attack, and system management to manage IDS data and the detector used.

articleTitle: Development of Inexpensive Microcontroller-Based Soil Moisture Measurement Device Implemented Using Time Domain Reflectometry
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Soil moisture measurement apparatus based on time domain reflectometry is considered expensive in Indonesian farming activities. To provide an economical time domain reflectometer that performs well for such applications, we develop a microcontroller-based soil moisture time domain reflectometer. Implemented on M4 ARM Cortex microcontroller, equivalent time sampling technique and delta sigma modulation was utilized to achieve a 10 pico-second resolution soil moisture meter working at frequency 1 MHz and expected to have accuracy below 1% of relative humidity.

articleTitle: Detection and Measurement of Object Distances Using the Combination Function of 2D LiDAR Sensor and Camera
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Automation systems in transport vehicles such as forklifts can provide solutions in terms of time, quantity, and accommodation costs during operation, as conventional forklift operation requires drivers with specific certifications and qualifications. Automation in forklifts requires various control functions that utilize various types of data. Some functions needed in forklift automation include object detection and object distance measurement. Object distance measurement will utilize LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) technology, which offers high accuracy with a wide detection range and can be used at various scanning angles. Using 2D LiDAR for scanning can only provide output in the form of detection along a single horizontal line, so for three-dimensional object recognition, the system requires additional supporting sensors such as cameras. Object detection or recognition using cameras can be performed using deep learning applications with specific datasets of objects to be detected. Object detection is implemented using YOLOv5, while object distance measurement utilizes data fusion and projection from 2D LiDAR with camera data. In this system, object detection data is provided with a precision of 0.97945 using YOLOv5 model with type-m epoch 100, while the best distance measurement is achieved using the projection method from 2D LiDAR data to the camera with an error rate of 0.15%.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of River Water Quality Monitoring System with Microsatellite
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: This paper discusses the design of a remote water quality monitoring system using nanosatellites simulated using universal software radio portable (USRP). This research was conducted to overcome the problem of unreachable signals in rivers with distant and remote locations. To monitor water quality, a prototype ship will be built that can move automatically and is installed with water quality sensors. To connect between USRPs, an antenna operating at a frequency of 2.22 GHz is designed. Water quality data is sent by the USRP to the satellite, then from the satellite forwarded to the ground station. This ground station is assumed to be the Ministry of Environment (KMLH). The results of the monitoring data will be displayed on the website.

articleTitle: Fall Risk Detection Using Heart Rate Variability
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Falls are a significant public health concern, especially for the elderly and individuals with high blood pressure. The World Health Organization reports that falls are the second leading cause of unintentional injury-related deaths, claiming 684,000 lives annually and costing $43.8 billion in medical care. This study introduces a novel approach to prevent falls by analyzing Heart Rate Variability (HRV) in individuals with and without hypertension, using the Garmin Venu SQ 2 smartwatch. HRV data were collected from two female participants over a week, one with hypertension and one without. RMSSD and SDRR values were measured, reflecting parasympathetic nervous system activity and overall heart rate variability. Results showed that individuals with hypertension had lower RMSSD and SDRR values, indicating a higher fall risk, aligning with previous research. The study emphasizes the importance of reduced HRV as an indicator of increased fall risk in hypertensive individuals, contributing to fall prevention research and advocating for a comprehensive approach to reduce healthcare costs and enhance well-being in high-risk populations.

articleTitle: Investigation of Control Algorithm for Electromechanical Vehicle Active Anti-Roll Bar
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The present paper aims to address the issue of improving the roll stability of vehicles by employing an active anti-roll bar (AARB) controller. The AARB controller is established using MATLAB/SIMULINK based on the principle of Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) Controller, and the CARSIM software is used to build a testing environment. The evaluation is conducted through specific indicators of vehicle roll stability. A comparative simulation was conducted on the control system by changing the vehicle speed. The joint simulation of SIMULINK and CARSIM software verified the feasibility and correctness of the established model and control system. The simulation results analyzed using MATLAB software show that the AARB control system can improve the vehicle's stability. The significance of the AARB control algorithm for other active safety controllers in vehicles was also briefly explained. We highlight the future research direction of the control algorithm for the AARB controller on the importance and impact of intelligent algorithms on future research.

articleTitle: Adaptive Headlight Controller Using Multi Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Vehicle lights are one of the main components of a vehicle which have enormous benefits for supporting driving safety, especially at night. This paper introduces an adaptive headlight control system using several sensors to optimize vehicle lighting. These sensors include gyroscopes, environmental light sensors, and proximity sensors. This system can detect surrounding ecological conditions and driver behavior, and then change the headlamp light pattern according to needs. This system is designed to automatically adjust the angle, brightness level, and light pattern of the headlamps according to vehicle speed. This optimizes lighting in front of the vehicle without disturbing drivers of other vehicles. Test and simulation results show a significant improvement in driving comfort and safety at night. This system also has the potential to reduce traffic accidents and driver fatigue. The Adaptive Headlight Controller using multisensors is a step forward in vehicle lighting technology that aims to create a safer and more comfortable driving experience, as well as making a positive contribution to road safety.

articleTitle: Consideration of PMU Wide Area Monitoring Data Acquisition for Operational Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The implementation of wide area monitoring system (WAMS) for power system is being carried out in many electric utilities. Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) can be used to implement a WAMS and a power system defense scheme because of the accuracy of voltage or current measurement. However, there are several concerns in acquiring PMU data to implement any analysis in electrical power system. Several circumstances that need to be noticed in data acquisition from multiple PMUs are synchronization of data acquisition time, reporting rate effect, data sample acquisition, and data acquisition range. This paper discusses data acquisition issues and solutions before they can be analyzed to obtain an accurate result. Unlike other research, this research provides insight into data collection problems and solutions before they are analyzed. The solution for data collection problems has already been implemented in real power system analysis using PMU for WAMS analysis.

articleTitle: Producer Mobility in Named Data Networking: Handoff Latency and Packet Arrival Rate
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The impact of producer mobility on Named Data Networking (NDN) networks in dynamic networking environments increases, hence increasing the need for performance analysis. When producers move between locations or nodes, packet loss is high. Therefore, this study focuses on experiments and assessing producer mobility by implementing the Hybrid Indirection Method (HIM) to minimize the impact of packet loss on the handoff process. The objective is to examine the impact of producer mobility, considering two crucial parameters namely, handoff latency and packet arrival rate. The obtained results offer valuable insights into the advantages and obstacles associated with producer mobility. This study provides a complete analysis of producer mobility using the network simulator ns3 framework. The results show a significant improvement with the HIM method and has tremendously improved handoff latency and total packet arrival rate.

articleTitle: Behavior Tree of Agents in Multi-Agent System on Action Video Game
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Video game has its uniqueness as escapism because it have the capabilities to pull player's focus to theirs by utilizing many factors or could be called immersive. One of the factors is the behavior of Non-Player Character (NPC) or agents in multi-agent system. Programming behavior of agents could be a daunting and difficult task, especially when the behavior of agents is too complex and it could take too much time. That is why faster alternative but also capable to done the same task or even better were needed. And that is one of the reason behavior tree is popular, because it is easy to use and visually appealing, but how about its capability? In this study we will assess how well behavior tree convey immersive in an action video game. Action video game in this study serves as multi-agent system. We hope this study could lead as foundation to more studies about behavior of agents that is not only advance and complex, but also visually appealing, easy and ready to use for people in industry.

articleTitle: Implementing the Johnson Algorithm: A New Approach to ONOS Intent Path Forwarding
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: In this paper, we assess the ONOS-Intent Path Forwarding (ONOS-IPF) version 2, representing a pivotal progression in intent-based path discovery within network infrastructures. By substituting the Dijkstra algorithm with the Johnson algorithm, ONOS-IPFv2 pioneers an approach for pinpointing paths from a singular source to multiple endpoints, a departure from the antecedent one-to-one model. Our empirical results indicate that, though ONOS-IPFv2 doesn't eclipse its predecessor in performance metrics, it adeptly incorporates intent in packet forwarding and unveils a refined mechanism for path discovery and provisioning anchored in bandwidth considerations. Regarding end-to-end latency, ONOS-IPFv2 is congruent with its forerunner, particularly for packets exceeding 3,200 bytes, and remains on par with the default ONOS packet forwarding application. The integration of the Johnson algorithm heralds an auspicious trajectory for network strategies, enriching our comprehension and propelling advancements in the realm of networking technologies.”

articleTitle: Effect of HV Guard in Reducing Electric Field Intensity of Gas Insulated Switchgear Spacer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: As one of the most important parts of gas insulated switchgear, many technologies have been explored to reduce the electric field strength in gas insulated switchgear spacer. This spacer, despite acting as the secondary insulation in gas insulated switchgear, holds a very important role to hold the high voltage conductor and separate it with the grounded tank. Failure in the spacer could result in overall failure of gas insulated switchgear. One of such accessories is the High Voltage Guard. A bulged conductor acting as the HV Guard is placed nearby the surface of the spacer. This accessory is then tested with finite element simulation for 2 types of 1 phase spacer design, conical design and disk design. Each method is proven, electric field wise, could improve the performance of the spacer. Both electric field in the surface, mainly on the triple junction area, and inside spacer could be suppressed to around 15% to 20% in both conical design and disk design.

articleTitle: A Realtime Map Tracker for an Autonomous Tram: Design and Implementation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: This paper describes the design and implementation of a real-time map tracker. The real-time map tracker consists of two main subsystems: the communication system and the GUI system. The communication system utilizes a localhost server as a buffer memory, equipped with REST API methodology to retrieve position data from the localization system, and WebSocket connection to transmit the position data to the GUI system. On the other hand, the GUI system in the map tracker is composed of various modules that provide comprehensive visual map information on top of Open Street Map (OSM). It includes the current tram position, tram waypoints, spatial information points, and notifications for the user. The developed map tracker successfully provides visual map information with a real-time latency of approximately 1.048 ms. It retrieves real-time data from the backend system with the highest correctness reliability. The proposed real-time map tracker achieved the target notification radius within 50 meters.

articleTitle: Supervised Machine Learning Approach for Predicting Cardiovascular Complications Risk in Patients with Diabetes Mellitus
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Diabetes mellitus, particularly type-2 diabetes, remains a prevalent health issue, raising concerns due to its associated risk of complications. Among these, cardiovascular complications pose a significant threat, exhibiting high morbidity and mortality rates. Health screening plays a pivotal role in stratifying the risk levels of diabetes patients, facilitating proactive measures to prevent the progression of complications. As such, the primary objective of this study is to develop a predictive model system for assessing cardiovascular risk in diabetes patients. Our study used the Cardiovascular Disease dataset and conducts experiments with various supervised machine learning algorithms, such as Naive Bayes, decision tree, random forest, AdaBoost, and XG- Boost. The results reveal that ensemble learning algorithms based on boosting, particularly AdaBoost and XGBoost, outperform other supervised machine learning methods. However, even with the best performance achieved using the dataset, the accuracy stands at 0.71, and the F -1 score is 0.69, which is still acceptable for screening purposes. Although these results provide valuable insights, indicating individuals at higher risk for cardiovascular complications in diabetes, further improvements are needed to enhance early prevention strategies.

articleTitle: Character-Based String Matching Similarity Algorithms for Madurese Spelling Correction: A Preliminary Study
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The Madurese language lacks of spelling correction study. Spelling correction suggests a list of corrections for misspelled words or strings. Its process consists of two steps, i.e., generating a list of suggestion strings likely to be the expected correct string and then ranking them. Henceforth, the ones considered the best match are those on the top list. This paper compares five character-based string matching similarity metrics for Madurese spelling correction. The metrics are also known as edit distance metrics, as they work by computing the similarity between two strings based on the number of edit operations needed to transform a string to another. Experiment results show that Hamming performs the best by achieving 90% correction accuracy, followed by Damerau-Levensthein at 88%, Levensthein at 86%, Jaro-Winkler at 73%, and Jaro at 72%. However, the computation time of Hamming is longer than Levensthein and more comparable to Damerau-Levensthein. Hence, implementing those three metrics is worthwhile for further study of Madurese spelling correction.

articleTitle: Exploiting Heterogeneous Graphs with GCN for Drug Repositioning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: In the realm of health concerns, drug development remains a formidable challenge due to its historical intricacy and costs. Addressing incurable diseases necessitates effective drugs, making the search for new therapeutic uses of existing drugs, known as drug repositioning, an invaluable strategy. This approach streamlines research and development, reducing expenses, as the safety of these drugs has been previously validated in trials. Over the last decade, the medical data landscape has expanded exponentially, providing researchers with an abundance of open-source data. Over time, continuously open-sourced data has shaped a heterogeneous network based on disease information. Deep learning's strong data mining capabilities in graphs have been extensively tested, and it demonstrates reliable extraction abilities, particularly when dealing with sparse data in heterogeneous graphs. The structural complexities of heterogeneous graphs call for adaptive methods. Among these, the Graph Convolutional Neural Network (GCN) stands out as a stable and widely applied deep learning technique in various domains. GCN efficiently extracts node features from graphs, thereby furnishing robust data support, either directly or indirectly, for drug repositioning endeavors. Enhanced GCN algorithms have the potential to significantly improve the extraction of hidden insights pertaining to diseases and drugs within heterogeneous graphs. This advancement promises to further accelerate progress in the field of drug repositioning while leveraging the expanding repository of medical data.

articleTitle: Energy Planning and Utilization in the North Sulawesi Electricity System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Energy sector is one of the contributors to climate change besides forestry, environment, and transportation sectors. Then, the results of the COP 26 in Glasgow meeting states that Indonesia have a target to achieve Net Zero Emission (NZE) by 2060 if there is international support for funding and technology with some note that this project does not interfere with availability and affordability. In achieving the zero-emission target, the government is implementing five main principles, which include increasing the use of new renewable energy (NRE), reducing fossil energy, explore the use of electric vehicles in the transportation sector, increasing the use of electricity in households and industries, and utilizing Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS). In this paper several proposals can be made to further reduce production costs and reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the North Sulawesi system compared to Electricity Supply Business Plan by PLN which is called RUPTL. Two additional scenarios can be used for the proposal, which are addition of geothermal, solar and pump hydro to replace coal power plant and construction of North Sulawesi interconnection with Central Sulawesi. From the simulation results of the cost and carbon emission analysis between three scenarios, the scenario from RUPTL is the cheapest in terms of cost at 3.295 billion USD and the interconnection scenario is the smallest in terms of emissions, with CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions reaching 0 Mt.

articleTitle: System Dynamics Modeling to Simulate Policy Making for 5G Deployment in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: This research is expected to provide input on how to implement the fifth-generation mobile network (5G) in Indonesia. 5G is the next generation of wireless technology for mobile networks that has great potential for economic growth. This technology is far superior to previous wireless technologies in terms of speed, capacity, latency and overall network performance. The government as a regulator is expected to take the right policy in regulating the telecommunications industry to develop the economy and social society. Since its commercial implementation in 2019 to date, 5G deployment is still focused on urban areas. This is because 5G deployment is economically favorable in urban areas, and unfavorable in rural areas. This has the potential to widen the digital divide in the future. This research is conducted using the system dynamics method, which has a proven track record in identifying causal relationships in various problems and simulating them to determine their impact in the future. The use of system dynamics is expected to help decision makers in making policies related to the implementation of 5G in Indonesia. This research concludes that 5G has a positive effect on the economy. The government can promote 5G investment by offering tax incentives or implementing infrastructure and radio spectrum sharing policies.

articleTitle: Development of Machine Learning Subsystem in Intrusion Detection System for Cyber Physical System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The growth of cyber-physical systems (CPS) has caused a rise of cyber-attacks. These attacks such as Stuxnet have great social and economic impact. Research and development of intrusion detection systems have emerged to protect CPS. Many research results have found that anomaly-based IDS using deep learning models have high detection rates towards attacks on various datasets. However, these models are not usually integrated with a running CPS. In this study, we propose an IDS for Process Instrumentation Trainer (PIT), a CPS in Institut Teknologi Bandung. This paper focuses on the detection and model training functionalities and their integration towards the whole system. A comparison is done between multiple models. Trained models were tested on the Secure Water Treatment (SWaT) dataset and PIT dataset. Test results show that 1D-CNN has the best detection performance. The model was able to detect 29 out of 36 attacks on SWaT and 5 out of 5 attacks on PIT. However, robustness of the proposed IDS has yet to be tested towards adversarial attacks.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of ResNet101, InceptionV3, and InceptionResnetV2 Architectures for Cervical Vertebrae Maturation Stage Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The classification of cervical vertebrae maturity (CVM) plays a crucial role in orthodontic diagnosis and treatment planning. This study aims to evaluate the performances of bone maturity classification using three convolutional neural network architectures. The dataset used in this study utilizes the CVM-900 dataset which contains labeled cervical vertebrae x-ray images in 6 levels of bone maturation. Preprocessing was conducted by ROI cropping which results in three datasets: Crop C2-C4, Crop C2-C6, and uncrop. Then, to decrease the possibility of overfitting, the datasets are augmented with random translation and rotation. This work compares three pre-trained networks: ResNet-101, InceptionResNetV2, and InceptionV3. Each network has unique characteristics to improve performance in deep learning. Visual explanations of CVM stage classification from each model are conducted through Grad-CAM which leverages the gradient information to the target classes. We found that InceptionResNetV2 yields the highest accuracy across models and ROIs. It is shown that ROI affects model's performance. However, due to overfitting and the inability of our model to infer multiscale features, the increase in accuracy is not as significant.

articleTitle: The Usability of P2P-FLIP Framework for Teaching Programming via Flipped Classroom
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Programming is an important and core subject in computer science. Computational skills learned through programming can be used in many subjects across the computing field. However, there are various challenges faced in teaching and learning programming. High cognitive load for students, lack of prior knowledge, and lack of pre-class preparation are among the problems identified in the programming. Flipped classroom is a hybrid active learning method that is widely used in programming nowadays. A P2P-FLIP framework was developed specifically for lecturers as a guideline to implement the flipped classroom strategy in programming. The post-class part in the framework is the main difference compared to existing frameworks. The usability study was carried out to identify users' views on the framework. The framework is evaluated by 10 lecturers through a knowledge transfer workshop and focus group discussions. The results from the discussions concluded the P2P-FLIP framework has the potential to be used as a guideline for implementing flipped classroom in programming.

articleTitle: Smart Home Healthcare Technologies Based on IoT for Bedridden Patient: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Smart home healthcare technology has emerged as a promising solution for providing effective and personalized care to bedridden patients. By incorporating various smart devices and sensors into the home environment, healthcare providers can monitor the health status of patients remotely and intervene promptly when necessary. This paper presents a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) on smart home healthcare technology for bedridden patients. A search spanning five database sources (IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, Science@Direct, Scopus, and Web of Science) from 2018 to 2023 was conducted. This review highlights the key findings and trends in smart home healthcare technology for bedridden patients, including the benefits of such technologies, challenges faced, and future directions for research in this area. By promoting SLR methodologies enhances the quality and reliability of evidence in this field, facilitating the development of effective smart home healthcare solutions for bedridden patients.

articleTitle: Computer Vision-Based Hydroponic Lettuce Contour and Area Recognition System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Agriculture is a vital industry for the people of Indonesia, but there are several obstacles, including limited space in urban areas and inefficient conventional sorting and harvesting methods. Using computer vision to choose hydroponic lettuce that is ready to be harvested and a robotic arm to bring the selected lettuce yields, the produced system aims to solve this problem. The system's computer vision algorithms include color space conversion, intensity transformation, and an algorithm for following borders. This project's research methodology combines a quantitative approach with an experimental approach, which consists of conducting several trials on the built system. Several trials demonstrated that the computer vision software was able to accomplish the specified objectives. The average success rate of the developed computer vision system is 93%, while the average success rate of the robot arm is 85%.

articleTitle: A Cyber-Physical-Social System for Image-Form Air Quality Data: Citizens Participation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: In recent years, air pollution has become a major global concern due to its detrimental effects on human health and the environment. Traditional air quality monitoring systems provide valuable data but often lack citizen engagement and fail to capture the spatial and temporal variations in pollution levels.
