This paper proposes a novel Cyber-Physical-Social System (CPSS) framework that integrates citizen participation and image-form air quality data to enhance the monitoring and understanding of air pollution. The proposed system design empowers citizens to actively contribute to air quality monitoring, fosters social awareness, and enables informed decision-making for improved air quality management.

articleTitle: Human Activity Recognition Based on Wearable Devices and Feedforward Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) using wearable sensors has garnered significant attention in recent years. This technology can continuously track human activities which is essential for remote health monitoring, elderly care, and rehabilitation. In this study, we propose a simple feedforward neural network (FFNN) model equipped with four fully connected layers to enhance the accuracy of HAR. Experimental results conducted on the UCI-HAR (UCI Human Activity Recognition) dataset show that the proposed FFNN model achieve an accuracy and F1 score of 0.96. It outperforms other existing algorithms, which are K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and Support Vector Machines (SVM), highlighting the effectiveness of a simplified neural network architecture in enhancing HAR performance.

articleTitle: Effect of SMOTE for Sleep Stages Classification Using Decision Tree, K-Nearest Neighbor and Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: One of the main problems in the diagnosis of sleep disorders is the act of annotating the sleep stages on the recording results of each patient. The annotation of sleep stages is based on signal characteristics by the standardized assessment guidelines of Rechtschaffen & Kales (R&K) and the American Academy of Sleep (AASM). Currently, the annotation of sleep stages by experts are manually conducted. Therefore, annotating the signal data takes a long time, between 8 to 20 hours for each patient. In addition, the manual and extended annotations can undoubtedly affect the eyesight of the experts, which can cause errors in annotating the stages of sleep. Therefore, this study develops a sleep stage classification system using Machine Learning (ML). This study discusses solving the imbalance problem in Physionet Sleep EDF data and selecting the proper sleep stage classification model for optimal accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. Combining the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) and Random Forest (RF) model yielded the best classification. The result of accuracy with annotations W, N1, N2, N3, and REM is 99%, 99%, 98%, 99%, 100% then sensitivity is 100%, 99%, 95%, 97%, 100%, and specificity is 99%, 99%, 99%, 98%, 100%.

articleTitle: VidyaMedic: Smart Alert System For Continous Vital Sign Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The proposed smart system namely VidyaMedic utilizes continuous heart rate monitoring through sensors, with data transmission to the cloud via an IoT platform. Testing was conducted on a 40-year-old male participant who wore the Polar H10 heart rate monitor for 24 days. The heart rate profile captures the circadian rhythm, the natural internal biological clock governing cardiovascular and behavioral processes over a 24-hour cycle, influencing morning, daytime, and nighttime activities. Health conditions can be assessed using an algorithm which calculates the running sum of standard deviation for heart rate data over this period. Initially, standard deviation is computed for each data point, quantifying data dispersion from the mean. Subsequently, the running sum of standard deviation enables the detection of significant changes over time, abrupt fluctuations indicate outliers or extreme values, potentially impacting overall standard deviation and signaling significant data changes. Deviations from the expected or previous standard deviation values, marked by a regression coefficient less than or greater than 1, may suggest cardiac abnormalities or heart rhythm disturbances.

articleTitle: Automation Lamp Healing Application based on Face Expression Identification System using Convolution Neural Network (CNN)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The disruption of routines, education, recreation, as well as concerns about family income and health, has left many young people feeling fearful, angry, and worried about their future. In this system, a smart system will be developed that can capture, process, and interpret facial expressions so that a person's emotions can be easily and accurately identified, which is one of the best solutions. The system will use artificial intelligence that has been trained beforehand using suitable datasets. In the processed of developing the system, Face image with the size of 48 x 48 x 1 became the input of the system, processes by Convolution layer using Relu activation function. The activation function used in the output layer is softmax because it is suitable for more than 2 classifications. by applying CNN based on Adam optimization which have result on 98.96% and 70%, for training and testing accuracy, respectively. Furthermore, the system accurately turn-on the healing lamp based on the emotion identified.

articleTitle: Optimization of Boosting Classifier Method for Paddy Growth Phase Classification Using Oversampling and Hyperparameter Tuning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The agricultural sector has a significant contribution to the achievement of the second Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which are zero hunger, ensuring food security, enhancing nutrition, and fostering sustainable agriculture. This goal is in line with the regulation issued by the Indonesian Government No. 68 of 2002 regarding food security. To achieve that goal, it is necessary to have timely and accurate agricultural data available. Machine learning can predict paddy growth phases more quickly and efficiently. In this study, the optimization method was carried out on the machine learning Boosting Classifier with the aim of this study being to find out which optimization method has the best performance on the Boosting Classifier model in classifying rice growth phases based on the evaluation results of 7 comparative metrics namely overall accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, kappa score, cross-validation, and time execution. The optimization Boosting Classifier algorithm is carried out using the hyperopt hyperparameter tuning method, imbalance data handling, and a combination of hyperopt hyperparameter tuning and imbalance data handling. As a result, the hyperopt hyperparameter tuning method is a method that can improve the performance of the Boosting Classifier machine learning model in classifying paddy growth phases based on the results of the values in most of the comparison metrics (6/7 comparison metrics) which are on average higher by 0.04 when compared to the other three methods are the baseline method, the imbalance data handling method, and a combination of hyperopt hyperparameter tuning and imbalance data handling.

articleTitle: Empowering Secure and Cost-Efficient Blockchain Electronic Voting by Optimized ZK-SNARK Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Electronic voting systems are crucial for maintaining democratic principles and ensuring transparency in modern democracies. Initially designed for secure and decentralized record-keeping, blockchain technology holds significant potential for revolutionizing the voting process by providing tamper-resistant and auditable ledgers. To this end, our research proposes a robust blockchain platform to enhance the security and affordability of electronic voting. The platform's architecture leverages the innovative Zero-Knowledge Succinct Non-Interactive Argument of Knowledge (ZK-SNARK) algorithm to enhance privacy and security while minimizing computational overhead. By integrating ZK-SNARKs, we enable voters to prove their eligibility and vote correctness without disclosing their votes. Our proposed platform also incorporates circuit design optimizations and pairing-friendly elliptic curves, using efficient cryptographic curves like the alt_bn128 or similar options suitable for ZK-SNARKs. This approach ensures the integrity and authenticity of the voting process. This paper offers a comprehensive understanding of the challenges posed by traditional voting systems, outlines the architecture of the proposed blockchain platform, and details the optimized implementation of the ZK-SNARK algorithm. Our research aims to advance secure, cost-effective electronic voting systems that enable inclusive and trustworthy elections.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of Game Reviews on STEAM using BERT, BiLSTM, and CRF
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The Steam platform releases thousands of games almost every week, providing customers with many options, which require various considerations to make a purchase decision. Steam has features that can help consumers consider purchasing games, such as the help dashboard that provides information on game reviews and ratings. However, based on user input reviews, game ratings are still manual, which may cause human error and inaccurate results. To help gamers get the desired game information and increase customer purchasing power towards available games, sentiment analysis is one technique for classifying opinions. This study focuses on sentiment analysis of game reviews, which will result in classification into two classes, positive and negative. It will be measured for its performance based on the f1 score evaluation results. The proposed model that we created is to compare sentiment analysis models using the baseline Bi-directional Long-short Term Memory (BiLSTM), Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU), and fine-tuning Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer (BERT). We then propose another model, BiLSTM-CRF, by examining the effect of using the last four hidden states of BERT and comparing it with the last one hidden state of BERT to be used in the BiLSTM-CRF model. Based on the results of sentiment analysis models we developed for the ten most reviewed games on Steam, the BiLSTM model combined with CRF on the last four hidden states yielded the best performance, with an Fl score of 95.2 %. This score exceeds the baseline transformer-based model's Fl score of 88.0%. This is because combining BiLSTM and CRF allows the log-likelihood of the BiLSTM emission sample to be obtained more accurately so the model does not lose its context.

articleTitle: Implementation of Topic Modeling in the Analysis of Topic Trends in SDGs Goal 6 Research
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: SDGs Goal 6 is one of the crucial objectives within the SDGs framework, making fulfilling this goal highly significant as it determines the achievement of other SDGs. As a serious global issue, this goal can be addressed through scientific research and innovation. However, research on this goal is often not well-known, leading to a need for more connection between the academic world and practitioners in implementing available solutions. Consequently, identifying critical pathways through scientific research is essential to attain this goal effectively. One of the expedient approaches is the utilization of topic modeling, which also facilitates the analysis of research topic trends related to SDGs Goal 6. This study employs topic modeling on data sourced from SemanticScholar using the BERTopic method, which captures the comprehensive context of research articles. The research results indicate that studies focusing on SDGs Goal 6 are interconnected with other SDGs. The default BERTopic model, chosen as the optimal model, illustrates that there is a prevailing topic tendency in target 6.3 related to water quality.

articleTitle: The Effects of Extract Function Refactoring On High Cyclomatic Complexity Code Smell and Maintainability Index
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Software that operates actively needs to be adequately managed and maintained to avoid future problems. One of the problems in the software is the existence of code smells. A code smell indicates that a problem will, in turn, occur in the software's source code. OpenSID is open-source software used to create village administration websites. The detection carried out in this study shows that the OpenSID source code contains 32 code smells of High Cyclomatic Complexity type, which, if left untreated, can cause problems in the future. One of the problems is the reduced level of maintainability of the software. This research performs refactoring using the Extract Function method on a High Cyclomatic Complexity code smell to analyze what effect refactoring has on the code smell and its impact on the value of the OpenSID Maintainability Index. The research used the following tools: PHPMD, PHPDepend, and PhpStorm®. The results showed that after refactoring, the High Cyclomatic Complexity code smells were gone in some functions, and the average value of the OpenSID Maintainability Index increased from 37.0337 to 42.0912. Even though, in the end, the maintainability of this software is still in the category of difficult to maintain, this Maintainability Index increases to 13.66% has shown that the refactoring Extract Function method in code smells High Cyclomatic Complexity can increase the maintainability of this software.

articleTitle: Automatic Text Categorization to Standard Classification of Indonesian Business Fields (KBLI) 2020
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Indonesia used a Standard Classification of Indonesian Business Fields (KBLI) to classify and categorize economic activities and businesses based on their primary functions and outputs. Practically, to determine the economic activity of a worker, a questionnaire is designed using open-ended questions that generate free-form text responses, and then the enumerator manually selects the appropriate category of KBLI. In this study, we develop text classification models using machine learning and transfer learning approach to automatically assign the category of KBLI from respondents' economic activity descriptions through free-form text responses. The dataset consists of a pair of respondents' job descriptions and the category of KBLI derived from the tourism survey. Based on the evaluation, our transfer learning model from pre-trained IndoBERT trained on a large monolingual Indonesian corpus outperformed machine learning models but with slight differences.

articleTitle: Non-Dominated Sorting Differential Search Algorithm for Optimizing Regulatory-Metabolic Networks by Using Probabilistic Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Modeling in biology has given valuable insights and can be a guide for wet labs. The optimal prediction of a particular metabolite can be obtained by analyzing the genome-scale metabolic model of an organism. The technique that can be implemented is in silico gene or reaction knockout. Many algorithms were proposed to study the effects of genetic perturbations. One of them is a non-dominated sorting differential search algorithm and flux balance analysis (ndsDSAFBA). This algorithm can simultaneously predict growth and production rates based on reaction knockout. It also provides non-dominated solutions that are useful. However, the limitation of that algorithm is the huge combinatorial possibility and the lack of gene regulatory networks. To overcome it, this study proposed a strategy to integrate the regulatory network into the metabolic network for improving the ndsDSAFBA algorithm, called ndsDSAFBA-TFs knockout. The conditional probability approach is used in this study. The proposed improvement has been compared to the regular ndsDSAFBA. The results show that the ndsDSAFBA-TFs knockout outperformed the regular ndsDSAFBA for optimal prediction of the production rate of the succinic acid, namely 16.429 mmol gDW<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>hr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. Moreover, the combinatorial possibility is significantly lower than the regular ndsDSAFBA. Based on the results, the ndsDSAFBA-TFs knockout can be suggested becoming the development of the ndsDSAFBA algorithm.

articleTitle: Domain-Specific Language Model Post-Training for Indonesian Financial NLP
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: BERT and IndoBERT have achieved impressive performance in several NLP tasks. There has been several investigation on its adaption in specialized domains especially for English language. We focus on financial domain and Indonesian language, where we perform post-training on pre-trained IndoBERT for financial domain using a small scale of Indonesian financial corpus. In this paper, we construct an Indonesian self-supervised financial corpus, Indonesian financial sentiment analysis dataset, Indonesian financial topic classification dataset, and release a family of BERT models for financial NLP. We also evaluate the effectiveness of domain-specific post-training on sentiment analysis and topic classification tasks. Our findings indicate that the post-training increases the effectiveness of a language model when it is fine-tuned to domain-specific downstream tasks.

articleTitle: Informal Indonesian Part-of-Speech Tagger Using Hidden Markov Model and Normalization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Twitter is a social networking platform that can be used as resources to find information in real time. Twitter is one of the social media that does not have writing criteria, users are free to express their thoughts and send messages. There are many messages and tweets that use abbreviations, foreign words, local and mixed languages, which are characteristic of informal language patterns. Informal language patterns do not rely on Indonesian, making the process of annotating word classes less precise and influential on the level of precision. The use of POS Tagging in previous research can annotate word classes well in formal sentences. The problem in informal sentences is solved by the process of word normalization after the preprocessing stage, where informal words are converted into formal words then Part-of-Speech Tagging is carried out on each word in the sentence such as nouns, verbs, adjectives, etc. The dataset used was 846 words, with a informal word count of 99 words. With the Hidden Markov Model commonly used in machine learning as well as the word normalization process, the system is able to increase the resulting precision value, there is a significant increase of up to 10% in the precision produced.

articleTitle: Big Five Personality Prediction Based on Indonesian Tweets and Personality Test
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The integration of human resources and artificial intelligence has shown a growing interest in automatically predicting personality traits, particularly in recruitment. To contribute to this field, we propose a new method to assist human resource professionals in Indonesia to identify candidates' personality traits. Biases come from personality tests due to their question format and susceptibility to manipulation on this research, we propose an approach that combines personality tests using the BFI form, which measures OCEAN personality traits, with personality trait predictions derived from Twitter data. This research aims to create a personality prediction model and system that efficiently and effectively screens candidate personality traits in human resources. This research has developed a novel model that combines personality test results with tweets personality prediction with an impressive F1-macro performance of 98%.

articleTitle: Developing Interpretive Text Analysis for Corporate Culture Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Corporate culture is crucial to an organization's success, as it influences teamwork, productivity, efficiency, and customer service ability. However, there has yet to be a consensus on measuring corporate culture. Most tools used for measuring corporate culture are self-reported questionnaires, which are prone to faking. Projective evaluation methods, however, are less popular due to time-intensive administration and scoring, and the need for uniformity in interpretation. These disadvantages of projective assessment could be reduced through machine-based text analysis. We developed a text-analysis projective assessment for corporate culture using a case study of one Indonesia's State-Owned Enterprise, which has recently undergone significant organizational changes, including digital transformation. The processes of developing the tools are operationalizing the variables, creating a corpus for training the model, and evaluating the model. We found that the combination of Label Powerset and Linear SVC performs best among all combinations of multi-label classification approach and algorithm. Moreover, we discuss the possibilities of future works to improve the tool.

articleTitle: Towards Sustainable Higher Education: A Framework for Implementing Green IT Strategies
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The rapid development of technology highlights the growing importance of incorporating green IT concepts into organizations, including universities. As educational institutions heavily rely on information technology (IT) to facilitate teaching and learning activities, the escalating usage of IT can have detrimental effects on the environment if not managed appropriately. This research aims to develop a comprehensive framework to guide the implementation and evaluation of green IT strategies in higher education. Initially, an examination of the prevailing conditions and challenges of implementing green IT in higher education will be presented. This will be followed by the design and result of the proposed framework. The research outcomes are expected to provide valuable insights and practical guidelines for other universities seeking to adopt sustainable IT practices and reduce their environmental footprint.

articleTitle: Securing UAV Communication with TinyJAMBU Cryptography
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: UAVs rely on a crucial communication protocol for efficient data exchange with ground control systems. However, security challenges like cyber attacks and GPS spoofing threaten their operations. The purpose of this research is to develop and evaluate a secure communication system for UAVs, using the TinyJAMBU algorithm, in order to address these security challenges and enhance the resilience of UAV operations against cyber attacks and GPS spoofing. The proposed TinyJAMBU algorithm provides high-security solutions for UAV communication by incorporating encryption, decryption, key management, and authentication. To evaluate its performance, we do simulations and experiments as our approach. In conclusion, the proposed UAV communication system that utilizes the TinyJAMBU encryption can ensure data confidentiality of control data from the ground substation.

articleTitle: Indo LEGO-ABSA: A Multitask Generative Aspect Based Sentiment Analysis for Indonesian Language
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Aspect-based sentiment analysis is a method in natural language processing aimed at identifying and understanding sentiments related to specific aspects of an entity. Aspects are words or phrases that represent an aspect or attribute of a particular entity. Earlier studies have applied generative pretrained language model for aspect-based sentiment analysis. An example of this is the LEGO-ABSA framework, which effectively utilized these models, specifically in English-based aspect-based sentiment analysis. LEGO-ABSA uses a multitask learning and prompting approach to enhance model performance. However, the application of this approach has not been done in the context of Indonesian language. Therefore, this research aims to implement the multitask learning and prompting approach in aspect-based sentiment analysis for Indonesian language using generative pretrained language model. In this study, the Indo LEGO-ABSA model is developed, which is an aspect-based sen-timent analysis model utilizing generative pretrained language model and trained with multitask learning and prompting. Indo LEGO-ABSA is trained with a hotel domain dataset in the Indonesian language. The obtained results include an f1-score of 79.55% for the Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction, 86.09% for Unified Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis, 79.85% for Aspect Opinion Pair Extraction, 87.45% for Aspect Term Extraction, and 88.09% for Opinion Term Extraction. Indo LEGO-ABSA adopts the LEGO-ABSA framework that employs the T5 model, specifically mT5, by applying multitask learning to train all tasks within aspect-based sentiment analysis.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>All works can be visited in https://github.com/rdyzakya/IndoLEGO-ABSA

articleTitle: Innovations in E-Commerce Development and The Potential Disruptive Features
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The innovations in technology have open up new dimension of research interest capable of enhancing ecommerce practices. These emerging developments have extensively added to the awareness of ecommerce as a preferred platform to purchase goods and deliver services. With the frequent changes in ecommerce development, there is a need for a close attention to keep with the innovative trend and ensure business success and to understand constrains and takes advantage of its versatility in providing efficient and timely services. However, there is limited study on the technological innovation in ecommerce development despite its value-added potential as a competitive online shop. Little is known about the issues constraining successful adoption of e-commerce practices. In this study, promising innovations has been identified as potential path to improve ecommerce practice. The innovative trend of ecommerce development and factors contributing to ecommerce success provides depth of insight on potential ecommerce. Widely used factors to evaluate ecommerce websites quality were and the impeding effects of adopting disruptive innovations were highlighted. Finding of this study reveals that the development trends in ecommerce are promising and attractive. It becomes very clear that the future of ecommerce is very and will continue to improve with the innovation in technology.

articleTitle: Development of an ESP32-Based Tracker with XTEA-Encrypted Coordinates
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: This research was aimed at developing a distance detection device that used the ESP32 and GPS modules, and applying the XTEA cryptography algorithm to increase the security of the data transmitted over MQTT protocol. The method used in the development of this device was to design an electronic circuit consisting of two ESP32s with GPS modules connected to respective ESP32s. Location data from first ESP32 were received from the GPS module, which were directly encrypted with XTEA cryptography before being sent to the MQTT server. Furthermore, the data was received by the second ESP32 from MQTT, which also directly decrypted by XTEA cryptography. Then the decrypted location data was used to calculate the distance between both ESP32s with the Haversine formula. The system took <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25.3 \mu{s}$</tex> to encrypt and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$34 \mu{s}$</tex> to decrypt the coordinates data. Also it took only 0.6% difference on memory resource usage compared to procedures without encryption and 0.01% for the decryption. These data showed that this device is able to detect distances and provide an adequate level of data security with XTEA cryptography that ran very cheap and efficient. Thus, this device can be used in various applications that require distance measurement and data security.

articleTitle: GRAIN Algorithm Implementation for Lightweight Hardware-Based OTP Authentication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: This paper discusses the implementation of the GRAIN algorithm on ESP32 for hardware-based One Time Password (OTP) authentication. OTP is an authentication method that uses a random code valid for a single use and can enhance the security of authentication systems. ESP32 is a microcontroller platform that supports IoT application development and reliable wireless communication. The GRAIN algorithm was chosen for its high security and ability to generate unpredictable sequences of random numbers. OTP authentication using ESP32 can be applied to various IoT applications that require a high level of security. The implementation is done in the C language. The implementation results were tested using simulation software and ESP32 hardware to evaluate security and authentication quality. It is expected that this research will contribute to the development of authentication technology for IoT systems and other applications that require a high level of security. The conclusion of this research is the proposed OTP authentication hardware system is able to decrypts encrypted OTPs sent by an authenticator to an RFID card, using the ESP32 as a constrained device equipped with an OLED screen and a button. Furthermore, the authenticator generates ciphered OTPs based on GRAIN 128 and sends them to the hardware via an MQTT gateway, utilizing only 25 percent of available resources, making it suitable for constrained devices.

articleTitle: Design of Cyber Risk Calculation Methods Using Monte Carlo Simulation in Marketspace
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Cyber risk assessment in marketspace necessitates comprehensive calculations that rely solely on data, reducing subjective expert opinions. This research proposes a methodology that utilizes Monte Carlo simulation to achieve objective risk calculations. This research identifies various causes of cyber risk in marketspace, including human error and third-party intention. By developing a Monte Carlo simulation program, risk quantification is simulated, allowing for a thorough understanding of the relationship between input variables and resulting risk values. The results show that the probability distribution of risk values can be obtained using data on cyber events that have occurred. The resulting output can provide a wide and varied range of risk values using only data and estimated values of influential factors. The Monte Carlo simulation developed can also provide similar outputs when there are data limitations with their own restrictions.

articleTitle: Automatic Anti-Swing Gantry Crane Based on Gradient Descent Optimization Proportional Integrated Derivative (PID): A Comparison Simulation and Real Experiment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Transporting payload with precise swing angles and transfer times poses a challenging task in building construction, which is why gantry crane systems are extensively utilized. Various control strategies, including open-loop and closed-loop systems, have been proposed to tackle this issue. However, most of these controllers rely on a model and parameters specific to the crane system, making the process of modeling and parameter identification complex and time-consuming. To address this challenge, this work presents a practical and simulation control method for automatic gantry cranes, which is evaluated simulation and experimentally. The lab-scale Gantry crane is developed in this work, which consists of mechanical and electrical parts. Proportional Integral and Derivative (PID) and Proportional Derivative (PD) controllers which applied optimization method are implemented in the electrical part of the system. The PID and PD controller applied in controlled the position and swing angle, respectively. The Gradient Decent optimization method is the best optimization method in determining the parameter of the controller, since it has the best simulation performance in the output of the system. The experimental result is developed and compared between simulation and lab-scale Gantry crane hardware implementation part. The performance of experimental results is shown appropriately approaching the performance of the simulation result, with the approximately settling time.

articleTitle: Factors of Big Data Adoption by the SMEs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Big data technology is a disruptive change in information systems and is leading the future development of IT. This paper studies the influence of small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) adoption of big data services. We built a research model, including three levels and eleven variables on influence factors. We combined a resource-based view with TOE to put forward five factors at the organizational level. The hypothesis analysis showed that technical complexity, technology tests, and organizational size affect SMEs' adoption most, followed by observing tests and market competition. Also, relative advantage, technical compatibility, and market competition slightly affect willingness. Senior leadership support, enterprises' resource readiness, and government policy affect the intention to adopt big data. Finally, we summarize this research conclusion and develop some suggestions for developing big data services on both service providers' and SMEs'views.

articleTitle: Exploring Deep Learning for Improved MIMO Performance: A Design Research Methodology Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Utilizing a design methodology approach, deep learning is harnessed to enhance Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) system performance. Leveraging artificial neural networks, deep learning effectively addresses MIMO signal complexities, yielding optimized solutions and identifying future research directions. Notably, deep learning aids in predicting channel traits, refining MIMO systems, and end-to-end communication design. Recent focus includes channel estimation, beamforming, and MIMO detection. Distinguishing design thinking from design methodology, the former grasps user needs, while the latter offers a structured, systematic issue-solving avenue. Through this approach, deficiencies are recognized, leading to superior MIMO solutions via conceptual understanding, fit analysis, and apt design methodology. The study's aim is to enhance MIMO performance effectively.

articleTitle: Multistate System Reliability: An Overview for Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: In the field of power systems engineering, reliability refers to the generating capacity to supply continuous service and be able to meet the demands of electrical loads. Renewable energy such as wind power or solar photovoltaic has intermittent characteristics, which are not always available and unpredictable. Binary state system modeling is typically modeled with reliability block diagrams (RBDs), Markov processes, and Monte Carlo simulations. However, this two-state model does not reflect intermittent fluctuations and randomness of renewable energy. To find a suitable model, this article provides a review of multistate system reliability. The multistate system can represent the variability of intermittent energy sources. Conventional multistate systems can be solved using Monte Carlo simulation or Universal Generating Function (UGF). In practical engineering, there is uncertainty both from the system model and from the model parameters. The uncertainty of the system consists of aleatory uncertainty and epistemic uncertainty. Probability theory is well suited to measuring aleatory uncertainty. Epistemic uncertainty results from incomplete information, lack of knowledge, subjectivity, and degradation. Non-probabilistic models quantify epistemic uncertainty using interval theory, fuzzy theory, or Dempster-Shafer theory. Aleatory and epistemic uncertainties coexist together and form non-probabilistic multistate systems. This system is solved by the interval method UGF, fuzzy UGF, and belief UGF.

articleTitle: Development of User Interface for Red Tilapia Aquaculture Management System Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Even though technology in fish farming in Indonesia is still needs to improve, today's technological advances have made Indonesians use smartphones. Current technological advances have enabled us to measure water quality more modernly. The thing that needs attention is the application design that is suitable for managing water quality in red tilapia ponds. This work aims to develop an appropriate interface for red tilapia aquaculture management system applications on the Android and iOS platforms. This application was created using a user-centered design interaction design approach with usability goals good utility, and user experience goals helpful. The usability testing results show that the specified usability and user experience goals are achieved. In addition, the results of the user acceptance testing conducted showed that the five participants completed 46 of the 46 existing test cases. This indicates that the application is feasible and can be accepted by fish farmers.

articleTitle: Designing a Mindful Computerized Therapy Module to Reduce Depression
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The advantages of the latest technology offer good potential as intervention support in reducing mental health symptoms among youth. Technological interventions provide an alternative to this group who are always worried about the barriers of stigma and self-confidence when it comes to mental health problems. However, interventions through existing technology developed have a less effective impact when users are not interested in continuing to use the system. Therefore, this study designed a computerized mind therapy module for youth aged 19 to 24 years to self-manage mild depression. The methodology comprised of three phases, namely document analysis, brainstorming, and storyboard sketching to design the requirements of a computerized therapy module that considers the needs of youth users. The first phase involved document analysis of written and electronic materials from previous studies. The second phase is a brainstorming session on the content of the application module conducted with seven experts consisting of mental health professionals, and multimedia experts with more than 10 years of experience. And the third phase involves developing the computerized therapy module, and sketching storyboards for low-fidelity prototype development. The results of the study consist of a computerized therapy module and a low-fidelity prototype interface that was developed based on the youth's needs. The output of the study guides designers and developers in developing mobile applications for mild depression therapy that can help youth manage their mental health independently and as a first step before seeking treatment from professional help.

articleTitle: Real-Time Emotion Recognition Using CNN and OpenCV
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: In the educational environment, real-time emotion detection can provide valuable information for teachers and students to understand students' levels of engagement, satisfaction, and attention during the learning process. By using CNN as an efficient and flexible model and utilizing the OpenCV open-source library in implementing the model into the system, the system becomes a very useful tool for improving teacher-student communication in integrated learning. The evaluation results show that this model has a good performance in classifying emotions in general, although there are differences in performance between the different emotion classes. Pruning was also carried out using TensorFlow Model Optimization (tfmot) to reduce model complexity and produce a more efficient model. This model can provide better insight to teachers about student response and involvement in the learning process. The results open up opportunities for further development in improving the accuracy and reliability of the model. With efficient and reliable implementation, this model can be a valuable tool in supporting the learning process in various learning environments.

articleTitle: Development of Atmel SAM-Based Wireless Sensor Node for Bridge Structural Health Monitoring (SHM)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Monitoring the structural health of civil structures is an important research area for continuously monitoring the condition of structures and predicting possible damage. One example is bridge monitoring. To estimate the damage to the bridge structure, it is necessary to continuously monitor the modal parameters, namely the natural frequency of the structure. This is generally measured using the accelerometer sensor. The accuracy of the monitoring system depends not only on accurate sensors, but also on the wireless sensor network used to collect data and transmit it from the sensor nodes to the processing center. In calibrating the accelerometer sensor, we use the VCD21D vibration calibrator tool to test and calibrate the accuracy of the sensor. The experiment was carried out by comparing the accelerometer measurement results with the reference value from the vibration calibrator. The experimental results show that the accelerometer calibration works well, resulting in a maximum measurement error of about 0.3 %. In addition, we also tested WSNs (Wireless Sensor Networks) synchronization using the RBS (Reference Broadcast Synchronization) method with a synchronization error of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{2049.5}\ \boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{s}$</tex>. The experimental results show that the RBS method successfully synchronizes the sensor nodes in the WSNs accurately and efficiently. The time difference between neighboring nodes is measured in very small timescales (microseconds).

articleTitle: Swimming Style Recognition for Video Sequences Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Today, deep learning is pivotal in automating computer vision tasks previously handled by humans. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) excel in signal, image, and video processing. This study conducted experiments to create a CNN model classifying swimming video sequences (freestyle, breaststroke, butterfly stroke). Datasets were assembled from YouTube videos adhering to specific criteria for underwater views and pool-side monitoring. The study addressed challenges like camera viewpoint and noise. A 2DCNN architecture with two convolutional layers served as the baseline model, enhanced with a third convolutional layer. It achieved remarkable accuracy (99.29%), precision (99.38%), and recall (99.37%) using an input size of 64x64 for the swimClass0 dataset. This model was selected for validation against the UCF15 benchmark, achieving 97.11% accuracy, 97.11% precision, and 97.08% recall. The results highlight the superior performance of the proposed model compared to the comparative study.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Low Cost Air Quality Monitoring System Using Gateway and Cloud Server
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: This paper proposes a Low-Cost Air Quality Monitoring system using LoRa. Our system aims to monitor air pollutants, temperature, humidity, and assess the development of microorganisms in Bandung City. Our objective is to provide an affordable and efficient solution for monitoring air quality in urban areas. By utilizing LoRa technology, our system enables real-time data transmission and analysis, allowing for timely interventions to improve air quality. In addition, we consider the low-cost implementation and real-time data transmission by employing LoRa communication for data transmission. The system integrates various subsystems, including Cloud Database, Cloud Data Processing, Graphical User Interface, and the Access Point subsystem with Buffer Manager and Server Communication modules. This integration enables seamless data storage, processing, and visualization, ensuring user-friendly and convenient access to air quality information. We evaluated our system using the UEQ Handbook, and it received an average score of 1.468 on a scale of −3 to 3, indicating high usability and user satisfaction. In conclusion, our proposed Low-Cost Air Quality Monitoring System using LoRa demonstrates its effectiveness in providing real-time air quality data to users. The system's affordability, user-friendly interface, and reliable data transmission make it a valuable tool for both individuals and authorities in monitoring and improving air quality. For future works, we suggest expanding the system's geographical coverage, integrating additional pollutant sensors, and enhancing data analytics capabilities for more comprehensive air quality analysis.

articleTitle: Algorithm Analysis of Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting Decision Tree, and Random Forest for Classification (Case Study: West Java House of Representatives Election 2019)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: In an increasingly modern era, machine learning-based technologies offer solutions to everyday problems. Machine learning enables us to build models that process data and train them to provide predictive results. We call predictions with categorical labels ‘classifications’. We commonly use several basic models for classification, including Decision Trees, Support Vector Machines, Linear Regression, and so on. We can combine these basic models to create an ensemble model, consisting of a boosting algorithm and a bagging model. We will test these two types of algorithms on the profile data of the candidates for the HoR West Java in the 2019 legislative elections. In this paper, we compare the Random Forest bagging algorithm and the Gradient Boosting Decision Tree boosting algorithm. The Decision Tree algorithm is also compared as a baseline. Prior to the comparison, we conduct data pre-processing and data exploration to identify the data features that influence the winning label for feature selection. Furthermore, we address the data imbalance by using Borderline-SMOTE before training the model. We compare the test results based on the F1 score. Our findings reveal that the use of selected features and the Borderline-SMOTE1 sampler significantly improved the F1 score. Additionally, the best-performing model for predicting victory with the given data is the Gradient Boosting Decision Tree, with parameter tuning and using feature selection results, which achieved an F1 score of 0.7445

articleTitle: Automatic Early Detection System of Feverish Infectious Diseases in Indoor Public Areas
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: This paper introduces a 3-layer IoT architecture designed to automatically detect and identify individuals with feverish infectious diseases in indoor public areas. The architecture comprises the sensing layer, edge computing, and cloud computing components. Sensor modules capture facial images and body temperature, which are wirelessly transmitted to an edge device through MQTT for identification using machine learning techniques. Subsequently, the data is forwarded to a cloud server through HTTPS for storage, feedback generation, and presentation to authorized users. Each subsystem is meticulously designed to meet its specifications. We conclude the prototype's design and implementation are successful within a controlled condition. The proposed system is also viable for future developments such as attendance management, airport security, and others. However, the design and implementation process also exhibits certain limitations, notably concerning the reliability and uptime of the sensory module.

articleTitle: Hierarchical CNN Automated Hierarchy Creation Using Output Prediction Analysis With Misprediction Matrix
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Computer vision applications have been widely employed in critical areas. However, the classification performance of these applications has been hindered by low accuracy when dealing with small objects that possess low resolutions and are dominated by their surrounding object environment. This limitation arises from the fact that small objects are constrained by their limited pixel count, resulting in insufficient information for accurately describing the real object. Thus, the inclusion of external information, such as grouping similar classes into distinct groups, can effectively ascertain the overall context of the object class for classification purposes. Subsequently, a hierarchical-based CNN is constructed, incorporating different contextual information pertaining to various classes, thereby generating coarse-to-fine levels to enhance the classification. However, most datasets do not come with multi-level labels and manually creating them is tedious and requires expertise on the domain. In this study, we propose a discriminative detector for object context to facilitate the grouping of object classes. The analysis and evaluation of the misprediction matrix information aid in identifying the appropriate similar groups to be formed. The experimental results on the CIFAR-100 dataset containing 50,000 training images and 10,000 test images demonstrate the enhanced image classification accuracy achieved by our proposed model by almost 6% compared to the baseline model.

articleTitle: A Survey on Designs and Implementations of Virtual Private Network (VPN)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Technologies today are pushed to provide high quality solutions with minimal costs of operation, especially on network and its architecture. While some industries have some working spaces separated from their main office, it is considered necessary to provide private remote connection for workers accessing their corporate internal servers from remote space securely. Many designs, architectures, and methods used for implementing the commonly known virtual private network (VPN). And VPNs are now established for various scope of many great industries. Networks are being used not only for making two small networks with common nodes can reach each other, but also for connecting much bigger and previously unimaginable elements. Each of these designs has their own architecture and method, depends on their needs and use cases. This survey paper seeks many ways to design and implement the VPN and what scope of industries has been provided the functionality of VPN.

articleTitle: IoT and AI-Driven Conceptual Model of Museum Ecosystem
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Museum ecosystems need digital transformation to provide value added to museums. This study discusses the digital museum ecosystem conceptual model based on artificial intelligence (AI) technology and the Internet of Things (IoT). The new conceptual model integrates three elements of the museum ecosystem, people, collections & infrastructure, and museum services collaborating and communicating to achieve outputs in supporting the achievement of museum organizational goals through IoT and AI-based digital technology. The conceptual model describes various forms of implementing IoT and AI in the museum ecosystem for museum management along with the value added or results generated for museum management. The development of this ecosystem conceptual model into a physical museum has an impact on optimizing museum performance by providing value added in the form of convenience and prosperity for users and various museum stakeholders, especially in Society 5.0.

articleTitle: The Non-Invasive HbA1c Measurement Device: A Narrative Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: HbA1c is used for long-term glycemic control monitoring and diabetes risk complications assessment. Traditionally, HbA1c measurements have been invasive, costly, and uncomfortable. The development of a non-invasive HbAlc measurement method holds promise in reducing discomfort and lowering the investment cost associated with the current testing instrument. This paper aims to review relevant literature to identify a suitable method for the upcoming research objectives, which involves providing accurate measurements through a non-invasive approach with the lowest possible cost. The paper begins by classifying fundamental approaches, acquisition technologies, and other factors that can inform further study. The direct approach and optical methods using multiple sources were selected for development, while correlation analysis and Bland-Altman analysis were identified as the most feasible validation methods.

articleTitle: Enhancing Data Logger Telemetry Security for Go-Karts using GIFT-COFB Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: This study focuses on the implementation of the GIFT-COFB lightweight cryptography algorithm to enhance the security of kart telemetry, specifically for the steering angle and throttle position data. The selection of GIFT-COFB was based on its suitability for microcontroller systems such as ESP32. The communication channel utilized MQTT, and a simulation circuit was designed with a potentiometer to obtain data for the mentioned parameters. The ESP32 microcontroller was employed to handle encryption for publishers and decryption for subscribers, leveraging additional libraries such as PubSubClient and WiFi in the Arduino IDE. The evaluation demonstrated that the GIFT-COFB algorithm effectively encrypts and decrypts messages. However, it was observed that the encryption process(631,0667ms) resulted in longer execution times compared to non-encrypted data(12,75ms). Meanwhile, for QoS analysis, without encryption, an average throughput of 42.11Kbit/s, 0% packet loss, 34.95ms time delay, and 34.9095ms delay is obtained which is better than when encrypting with a throughput rate of 18.48Kbit/s. s, 0% packet loss, 108.148ms time delay, and 95.67ms jitter.

articleTitle: Estimation of Rice Harvested Area in the Rainy and Dry Seasons Using Remote Sensing Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The rice harvest area in Indonesia is influenced by the rainy and dry seasons, so data is needed as a reference for food security policies. Currently data collection is carried out through KSA surveys, but this requires quite a lot of human resources. Remote Sensing can be an alternative method for acquiring information about rice cultivation areas. This study aims to estimate the planted and harvested rice area in Sragen Regency, Central Java, during the 2021 rainy and dry seasons, utilizing Sentinel-2 MSI Level-2A satellite imagery data. The employed methodology encompasses Machine Learning techniques (Decision Tree, Bagging, Random Forest, and SVM), with Random Forest emerging as the most effective model. Evaluation of the model's performance in determining the planted area (rice field class) yielded an F1-score of 0,9154 for the entire year, 0,886 during the rainy season, and 0,9651 during the dry season, with estimated planted areas of 30.204,48 ha, 31.970,89 ha, and 32.719,39 ha, respectively. The evaluation results of the estimated rice harvest area model are the F1 and MAE scores, 0.8385 and 7.024 per month. The estimated harvest area for the rainy and dry seasons is 22,033.47 ha and 23,656.45 ha.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>979-8-3503-8129-0/23/$31.00 ©2023 IEEE

articleTitle: Collaborative Online Learning Framework to Cultivate Parent-Teacher Engagement in Primary School
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Parents' commitment and engagement are crucial elements in collaborative online learning (COL). The continuous support provided by teachers and schools can foster parent-teacher engagement within the school community. Such engagement from parents yields benefits for both the school and students, leading to improved performance and academic achievements. However, several barriers hinder parent-teacher engagement, including parental commitments, time constraints, limited digital literacy, technical and communication skills, and diverse cultural backgrounds. To address these challenges, technology and various communication methods, such as social media and online learning platforms, have been recognised as potential solutions to enhance parent-teacher engagement. Therefore, this study aims to overcome these barriers and provide solutions by introducing the COL framework for cultivating parent-teacher engagement at primary school. This study reveals this framework's effectiveness in promoting continuous parent-teacher engagement.

articleTitle: Handling of Indonesian-English Codeswitching Speech in End-to-End Indonesian Speech Recognition System Using Connectionist Temporal Classification Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Code-switching in speech poses a significant challenge to Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems. When left unaddressed, code-switching between languages can lead to decreased speech recognition accuracy. With advancements in technology, ASR systems have evolved into two main architectures: conventional and end-to-end (e2e). Compared to conventional architectures, e2e architectures are more commonly used due to their simplicity and superior performance. A widely used modeling technique in e2e ASR is the Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC), which combines Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) with the CTC loss function to handle situations where the alignment between speech and transcription is unknown. This study focuses on handling the code-switching phenomenon between Indonesian and English in e2e ASR using the CTC model. The proposed code-switching handling involves pre-training and transfer learning. Pre-training is performed on Indonesian speech data, resulting in an average error rate of 13.23% (WER) and 4.13% (CER) on Indonesian test data. However, the error rate remains high for code-switched test data. Transfer learning is then conducted on code-switched speech data by fine-tuning the model. This results in improved performance, with an average error rate of 48.115% (WER) and 16.8% (CER) on code-switched test data. Nonetheless, the error rate on Indonesian test data increases. To address this, a two-model CTC system is developed, capable of distinguishing between Indonesian-only and code-switched data using confidence values. The 2-model system successfully reduces the average error rate to 24.6625% (WER) and 7.0525% (CER) for Indonesian data and achieves 53.852% (WER) and 20.7675% (CER) for code-switched data.

articleTitle: Application of User-Centered Design Approach in Developing Interaction Design of In-Kind Donation Feature on a Crowdfunding Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The rapid advancement of technology has had a profound impact on human life, driving the need for faster and more effective social activities, including donation practices. One notable example of technological progress is the emergence of social crowdfunding platforms, which have revolutionized the way donations are made. However, the integration of in-kind donation features, specifically donating goods, remains relatively limited on crowdfunding platforms, as they predominantly focus on managing monetary contributions. Nonetheless, there are segments of the population who require the donation of goods due to difficulties in managing unused items and a preference for ensuring that donated items serve their intended purpose. This background necessitates the development of an interaction design for incorporating the donation of goods on crowdfunding platforms. The primary objective of this research is to explore and identify the challenges and design considerations related to digital donation features for goods. Employing a user-centered design approach, based on the ISO 9241-210:2019 method, the study follows a four-stage development process that prioritizes user needs and preferences. The culmination of this research effort is a high-fidelity interactive prototype that achieves usability goals related to effectiveness and utility, as well as user experience goals associated with helpfulness and enjoyment. The evaluation of the prototype's effectiveness and user experience employs usability testing methods, including interviews, Single Ease Question (SEQ) surveys, and the System Usability Scale (SUS). The results of the second iteration of testing indicate that the constructed interaction design successfully addresses the predefined usability and user experience goals. Moreover, this phase of testing generates valuable insights that can inform future design recommendations.

articleTitle: Super-Resolution in Sparse Representation Fusion for Medical Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The application of super-resolution techniques enhances the quality of low-resolution images. The present study investigates the application of the super-resolution technique in the context of sparse fusion systems. This research integrates low-resolution functional anatomy positron emission tomography (PET) images with high-resolution structural anatomy magnetic resonance (MR) images in order to enhance the overall resolution. The fused image exhibits enhanced resolution and encompasses a greater amount of both structural and functional anatomical details. The simulations demonstrate that our proposed methods yield significant improvements. The mutual information feature increases from 0.85 to 0.92, the objective image fusion performance increases from 0.60 to 0.62, the edge strength for edge preservation also increases from 0.87 to 0.95, the mean squared error (MSE) decreases from 2.74E-04 to 1.85E-05, and the Pearson absolute correlation coefficient also decreases from 5.3E-03 to 2.6E-03.

articleTitle: Backend System for Nile Tilapia (Oreochromis Niloticus) Cultivation Management System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Water quality is an important factor in nile tilapia cultivation. The level of water quality can be determined by the physiochemical parameter of the water. The health and quality of nile tilapia are highly influenced by the quality of water they live in. A mobile application management system for nile tilapia cultivation is used to monitor and provide action recommendations for nile tilapia cultivation ponds and its water quality. This system utilizes smart water meter as an implementation of IoT (Internet of Things) to determine the values of physiochemical parameters of the water. A backend system is required to support the management system through a server, ensuring the load will not be burdened by the user's mobile device. Smart water sensor data is integrated through Antares, a cloud IoT platform in Indonesia. It is used as a broker to connect and send data to the backend system, giving a real-time data. The backend system is connected to a machine learning component to provide predictions regarding water quality parameters, providing anticipatory actions and notifications to users. The system is tested for its functionality and performance in handling loads. The test results shows that the architecture of the backend system plays an important role in supporting the application's functionality to operate optimally.

articleTitle: Designing Big Data Management Policy for Statistics Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Technological developments and urbanization are becoming a reality we must face today. Both of these phenomena bring challenges that must be faced related to data. The International Data Corporation (IDC) estimates that the volume of data worldwide will increase fifty times from 2010 to 2020. It is estimated that the volume of global storage will double every 12–18 months. Most of the data is unstructured. This situation is known as the big data phenomenon. The challenges related to big data are opportunities for statistical organizations to produce more accurate and fast official statistics. In implementing big data as one of the new data sources, Statistics Indonesia (BPS) needs to pay attention to big data management aspects because there are risks that can lead to lawsuits, decreased reputation, and loss of public trust. Traditional governance is insufficient to address the new issues big data brings. A literature study on data management and governance at BPS shows no specific research on big data management. This research seeks to answer these problems by providing solutions by designing policy artifacts. Policy is important in implementing information and communication technology and is the foundation for building all information technology services. The definition of policy used in this study is a document established by the organization's leadership board that explains what must be done and what cannot be done, must be obeyed, is binding, and contains elements of sanctions for policy violations. The methodology used in this study is the Design Science Research Methodology (DSRM). The conclusions from this study indicate that a new artifact has been produced in the form of a big data management policy that meets the criteria of completeness, ease of implementation, ease of understanding, and provides environmental benefits for BPS.

articleTitle: Gamification Adaptive Elements in Virtual Learning to Improve Behaviour and Collaborative Interaction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: A crucial aspect of virtual learning is an adaptable and dynamic environment that can adjust to individual learning strategies, encouraging positive behavior change while simultaneously maintaining motivation to learn. Research has demonstrated that gamification techniques can enhance learning effectiveness by incorporating motivational and enjoyable elements. This technique utilizes game mechanics, including competition among students to achieve recognition. However, implementing gamification techniques can lead to individualistic and competitive behavior among students when completing tasks. This emphasis on rewards can negatively impact collaborative interactions between students, which is critical for engagement in virtual learning and future workplace success. Consequently, this study aims to develop adaptive gamification elements in virtual learning that can promote collaborative behavior and maintain student motivation. The findings of this study shows that gamification elements such as leaderboard, badges, points, rewards, challenges, feedback, progress bars and level can be implemented for developing a virtual learning model based on students' learning style.

articleTitle: Depth and Pitch Control of Autonomous Underwater Glider Using Model Predictive Control with ARX Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Autonomous Underwater Gliders (AUGs) are extensively developed vehicles capable of prolonged exploration and observation in complex marine environments. Control of the AUG is challenging due to its slow response system and its constraints. In this research, a linear model representation of AutoRegressive eXogenous input (ARX) will be constructed using input and output data from the AUG system, built Model Predictive Control (MPC), analyzed the performance, comparing with traditional Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID). The objective is to enhance setpoint tracking accuracy and minimize energy to extend exploration time while faced with constraints. Simulation results reveal MPC exhibits potential setpoint tracking, low overshoot as low as 0.6% up to 0.3m/s maximum depth rate, has relatively low input changes indicating good efficiency compared to PID. MPC approach effectively addresses slow response systems, managing momentum, and handling actuator constraints commonly encountered in AUG.

articleTitle: Exploring AI and Islam in Indonesian Education: An Anthropological Inquiry
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Indonesia, as the world's most populous Muslim nation, finds itself at a pivotal juncture in the realm of technological advancement. Recognizing the profound impact of emerging technologies, especially Artificial Intelligence (AI), on its trajectory is of utmost importance. While AI and Islamic beliefs may initially seem distinct, they share a common theme: an orientation toward envisioning future possibilities. Employing a blend of multimodal and mixed research methods, our objective is to scrutinize and draw comparisons between narratives and visual representations of AI's influence on religious prospects, particularly within the higher education landscape of Indonesia. We propose to investigate the curriculum, teaching practices and careers of young AI-professionals at Indonesia's oldest secular state university, namely Institut Teknologi Bandung (ITB), as well as Indonesia's first Islamic state university, namely Universitas Islamic Negeri Syarif Hidayatullah Jakarta (UIN-JKT). Notably, both institutions have recently introduced AI programs, making them rare in this regard. In this STEM-focused context, shedding light on the societal implications of AI education within Islam takes on heightened significance, with a focus on challenging Western-centric perspectives and contributing to a decolonization-centered research narrative. As this project is still in its early stages, this short paper will discuss related work and propose future directions to study Indonesia's AI-Islamic-educational future(s).

articleTitle: Development of a Bird Song Identification Model Using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Birds have a very large number of species that show remarkable diversity, but this diversity is threatened due to human activities and natural phenomena. Identifying bird species that still exist in an ecosystem is an initial action that can be taken to protect this bird diversity. In this study, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model was built to automate the process of identifying bird species in bird song data. In the experiments conducted, 24 CNN models were built, which had differences in architectures, feature extraction techniques, and types of input data. There are three architectures used: AlexNet, DenseNet, and VGG. There are four feature extraction techniques used: mel-spectrogram, harmonic component-based mel-spectrogram, percussive component-based mel-spectrogram, and MFCC. As for the types of data used, there are two: data that has been cleaned (clean data) and data that has not been cleaned (raw data). Based on the experiment's results, the CNN model with the best performance is obtained with the DenseNet architecture, feature extraction with percussive component-based mel-spectrogram, and clean data as model input. This evaluation process is carried out using two types of testing methods: testing using chunk data and testing with complete data. The accuracy of the best model reaches 85.67% for testing with chunk data (method 1) and 90.42% for testing with complete data (method 2).

articleTitle: A Spatio-Temporal Neural Network Approach for Predicting Traffic Accident Hotspot Areas: A Case Study in Bandung City
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: Traffic accidents are the most significant cause of human death after disease, with the majority of victims being of productive age. In order to decrease the number of traffic accidents, it is crucial to identify where and when they occur most frequently. The Spatio-Temporal Neural Network (STNN) approach is a reasonably new yet superior method for modeling space-time data. However, this method needs to be improved to deal with the limitations of spatial datasets related to traffic accidents in Bandung. The primary focus of this study is to enhance the performance of STNN in producing forecasts regarding traffic accident hotspots. Several experiments have been carried out, including conducting experiments with several zoom levels, comparing STNN with traditional machine learning methods, and applying GetisOrd Gi* to the dataset. The results showed that using the GetisOrd Gi* approach provides an additional advantage in improving the predictive result of STNN.

articleTitle: Exploring Software Development Waste and Lean Approach in Green Perspective
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: There has been growing attention to software development, waste reduction, and environmental sustainability. The Lean approach was developed in the manufacturing industry and used for software development by reducing waste and increasing efficiency. This approach has been called “Green Lean” in the context of environmental sustainability. Green Lean software development aims to reduce waste in the software development process while minimise the environmental impact of software development. This method identifies and reduces the seven types of waste specified as overproduction, defects, waiting, overprocessing, motion, inventory, and talent. Green Lean software development also promotes sustainability throughout software development. It educates the developers about sustainable development practices to ensure environmental sustainability can be considered when making decisions throughout the development process. Besides, Green Lean software development aims to eliminate waste and grow productivity in the software development process while considering each activity phase's environmental impact. This approach can help reduce software development's environmental impact and improve the final product's quality.

articleTitle: Car Engine and Chassis Assembly Training Simulation Using VR Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICEEI)
abstract: The process of educating and learning about the automotive industry is still ongoing, and one of the most effective techniques is the provision of direct practice. Such a system is regarded as effective, albeit with certain downsides. One of them is the restricted area and time required to conduct the exercise, as well as the significant risk of accidents during vehicle engine assembly. Based on these justifications, Vehicle Engine Assembly Simulation with Virtual Reality (VR) Technology is now available as an alternate means of educating students about the automotive industry, particularly car engine assembly. This concept employs a virtual environment that allows users to perceive the automobile world in real time through an immersive experience. VR allows users to directly disassemble automobile engines. This virtual reality application was created utilizing the Oculus Quest 2 platform and the Unity Game Engine.
